【133】1\. Gottron Papules 2. Plane Warts
----------------------------------

【134】The Gottron papules of dermatomyositis, when affecting exclusively or mainly the back of the hands, should be differentiated from plane warts, which need a different treatment. The differential diagnosis is even more difficult when plane warts on the back of the hands affect a patient with dermatomyositis.

|  | 1\. Gottron Papules | 2\. Plane Warts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Definition | Papular lesions due to inflammatory changes of the dermis. | Epidermal papules induced by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and characterized by acanthosis and epidermal hyperkeratosis. |
| Location on the hands | Back of the hands, particularly at the level of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. | Back of the hands without predilection for the surfaces covering the joints. |
| Lesion distribution | Symmetrical. | At least initially, they are more prevalent on one hand. |
| Other sites to be affected | Extensor surface of the elbows and knees. | Face. |
| Koebner phenomenon | Rare. | Frequent. |
| Other cutaneous findings | Heliotrope erythema, psoriasis-like lesions on the extensor surface of the elbows and knees. | None. |
| Other findings | Clinical and laboratory findings showing muscle involvement. | None. |

【136】### Diagnostic Summary

【137】Gottron papules : symmetrical and periarticular; they are associated with other signs of dermatomyositis.

【138】Plane warts : initially asymmetrical without predilection for the joint surfaces.

【101】**Case Study Analysis**

【102】The advanced practice provider performs the assessment and physical examination on the patient and describes 36 hours duration of unilateral pinkeye with crusting. Left eye exhib-its mild but diffuse injection， including injection of the tarsal conjunctiva. The child also exhibits a copiously runny nose. Her history and examination are notable for the absence of periorbital edema or eye pain. On fluorescein examination there is no uptake of dye to suggest a corneal abrasion. Visual acuity is 20/20.

【103】Considering the recent history of a URI， persistent nasal drainage， and ongoing wiping of the eye， allergic conjunctivitis most likely can be ruled out. The symptoms are most likely not caused by an injury or blepharitis. Other potential causes for conjunctivitis can be ruled out based upon the patient's age and symptoms.

【25】**Disease Definition**

【26】一Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder is an indolent lymphoproliferativeedisorder characterized clinically by a solitary skin lesion (without patches/plaques typical of mycosis fungoides) and histopathologically by a cutaneous infil-trate of small- and medium-sized pleomorphic CD4-positive T cells (Table 29.1).

【27】**Epidemiology**

【28】Usually adult and elderly patients， but pediat-ric cases may occasionally occur.

【29】**Preferential Sites of Involvement**

【30】\- Face (central face， forehead).

【31】**一Neck.**

【32】\-Upper trunk.

【33】**Ear.**

【34】**ClinicalFeatures**

【35】\- Solitary plaque or nodule/tumor (Fig. 29.1).

【36】\-EErrythematous or purplliisshh surface without ulceration. Slow growing.

【37】\- Absence of patches and/or plaques typical of mycosisfungoides (must be excluded clinically).

【38】一 _Less common presentations： more than one_ lesion but in a localized area. If multiple widespread lesions occur， consider another diagnosis.

【39】**Histomorphology**

【40】_一_ Pattern： dense， diffuse and/or nodular， superfi-cial and deep dermal infiltrate (Fig. 29.2). Epitheliotropism is usually not prominent； however， focal exocytosis of lymphocytes may be observed in the epidermis and hair fol-licles (Figs. 29.3 and 29.4). Ulceration， promi-nent necrosis， or angiodestruction is not seen.

【41】一1Less common patterns： plaque-like superficial and mid-dermal infiltrate. Variable extension into superficial panniculus.

【42】一Neoplastic cells： small- and medium-sized lymphocytes. While smalllymphocytes predominate， a significant component of irregular，hhyperchromatic (pleomorphic) medium-sized lymphocytes should be present(Fig. 29.5). Large lymphoid cells with vesicu-lar chromatin and prominent nucleolus should be rare and scattered (<30% of the infiltrate).

【43】一1Reactive cells： histiocytes can be quite promi-nent (Fig.29.6). Occasional plasma cells and multinucleated giant cells.

【44】**Immunophenotype**

【45】\- Neoplastic cells： the infiltrate consists pre-dominantly of CD3-positive alpha-beta T cells without significant expression of CD30 or CD56 (Fig. 29.6). There isa significant predominance of CD4 expression. Loss of pan-T-cell markers may occur (usually CD7， rarely CD5) (Fig. 29.7). Because of the T fol-licular helper (TFH) phenotype， there is fre-quent expression of PD1 (CD279) by atypical lymphocytes，oftenarranged nclusters(Fig. 29.8). Other TFH markers may be expressed (BCL6， CXCL13， ICOS， rarely CD10). The Ki-67 proliferation index is low(below 50%) (Fig. 29.9).

【46】_一1_ Reactive cells： small subset of predominantly small reactive CD8-positive T cells. While T cells predominate， a significant component of reactive CD20-positive B cells is generally present (Fig. 29.10). Variable component of CD68-positive histiocytes. Occasional poly-typic plasma cells. CD21 is generally negative since1lymphoid follicle formation is uncommon.

【47】**Genetics**

【48】一上Monoclonal rearrangement of T-cell receptor genes in majority of cases.

【49】_一_ EBV (EBER in situ hybridization) is negative.

【50】**Prognosis**

【51】**_一Excellent.Rare local recurrence._**

【52】一Because of its indolent behavior，“lymphopro-liferative disorder is the currently preferred term rather than“lymphoma.”

【53】_一_ 5-year survival： close to 100%. The initially reported 5-year survival of 75% has not been observed in subsequent series； it appears that the initial series may have been contaminated by systemic lymphomaspresenting iin the skin.

【54】一1Adverse risk factors： cases incorrectly classi-fied：1recurrence/progression afterinitial treatment.

【55】**Differential Diagnosis**

【56】Pseudolymphoma. Primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoprolifer-ative disorder has similar features and benign behavior analogous to cutaneous T-cell pseu-dolymphoma with nodular growth pattern. It is conceivable that it may represent a clonal variant of the latter.

【57】_一_ Cutaneous Leishmaniasis may cause diagnos-tic confusion since it often presents with a solitary lesion on exposed skin that lasts sev-eral months and often demonstrates cutaneous infiltrates with prominent lymphocytes and histiocytes (Fig. 29.11). However， the infil-trate is generally more granulomatous and more plasmacytic than in primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphop-roliferative disorder. In addition， ulceration and Leishmania organisms would be absent in primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder. Careful examination of superficial dermal histiocytes at high-magnification is recommended.

【58】\- Primary cutaneous marginal zone B-cell lym-phoma may have features similar to primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder： indolent behav-ior， frequently solitary nodular skin lesion， presence of mixed dermal infiltratesVwith

【59】prominent T-cell and B-cell populations， and frequent PD1 expression (Figs. 29.8and29.10). However， marginal zone lymphoma lacks a significant component of hyperchromatic pleomorphic medium-sized cells and is generally associated with lym-phoid follicles and monotypic plasma cells. In contrast， prominent lymphoid follicles would be an unusual finding in primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphop-roliferative disorder. Plasma cells are uncom-mon and polytypic in primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphop-roliferative disorder.

【60】一Cutaneouspresentation of ssystemic T-cell lymphoma.Systemic T-cell1lymphomas(which may have T follicular helper pheno-type) may occasionally present in the skin and may closely mimic primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoprolifer-ative disorder. Therefore， adequate staging at initial diagnosis and/or close follow-up would be judicious to exclude this possibility. This differential is important because of the signifi-cantly worse prognosis of systemic T-cell lymphoma.

【61】\- Mycosis fungoides. As part of the definition of primarycutaneousCD4-positiveesmall/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder， mycosis fungoides must be excluded clini-cally by the absence of patches and/or plaques. This distinction is critical because of the sig-nificantly worse prognosis of tumor-stage mycosis fungoides. By definition， a patient with mycosis fungoides can never be subse-quently diagnosed with primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphop-roliferative disorder (if a similar lesion devel-ops in a patient with known mycosis fungoides， theediagnosis is tumor-stage mycosis fungoides).

【1】### Prognosis and Therapy Considerations

【2】Solid papillary carcinoma without areas of conventional invasive carcinoma is currently staged and managed as non-invasive disease (Tis), despite occasional absence of myoepithelial cells and rare reports of metastases to axillary lymph nodes \[ 10 \]. Prognosis after excision is generally favourable. The presence of a solid papillary carcinoma pattern is associated with favourable clinicopathological parameters when evaluated among breast cancers with neuroendocrine differentiation \[ 11 \].

【3】Invasive Papillary Carcinoma
----------------------------

【4】### Definition

【5】Invasive papillary carcinoma is an invasive carcinoma with a papillary architecture in more than 90 % of the tumour. Invasive carcinoma without papillarity that is associated with encapsulated papillary carcinoma or solid papillary carcinoma should not be referred to as invasive papillary carcinoma; it should be subtyped according to the morphological appearance of the invasive tumour \[ 4 , 9 \].

【6】### Clinical and Epidemiological Features

【7】Invasive papillary carcinoma in its pure form is extremely rare, and there are no specific clinical or epidemiologic data.

【8】### Imaging Features

【9】Invasive papillary carcinoma may present as a radiological or palpable mass. Associated spiculations are rare, and abnormal microcalcifications may be seen on mammography. On ultrasound examination, a complex solid–cystic mass with papillary projections and internal echoes from cellular debris and haemorrhage may be observed, with ill-defined margins reflecting invasion. The solid components are commonly hypervascular on colour Doppler.

【10】### Pathologic Features

【11】#### Macroscopic Pathology

【12】These tumours have solid fleshy appearances that may be friable due to papillary formation.

【13】#### Microscopic Pathology

【14】Histologically, papillary fronds are seen in the tumour as it invades into surrounding breast parenchyma (Figs. 4.69 and 4.70 ). Stromal desmoplasia and inflammation may be present at the advancing tumour front. The presence of invasive carcinoma with another morphological subtype in more than 10 % but less than 50 % of the tumour warrants designation as a tumour of mixed pattern.

【19】### Differential Diagnosis

【20】#### Metastatic Papillary Adenocarcinoma

【21】As invasive papillary carcinoma of the breast is very uncommon, possible metastasis from other organ sites such as the lung (Fig. 4.71 ) and ovary should be excluded. Uncommonly, thyroid papillary carcinoma may also metastasise to the breast but should be recognised by the presence of colloid production and typical nuclear morphology. Immunohistochemistry is a useful adjunct in distinguishing metastatic papillary carcinoma from primary breast disease. However, there is a need to be aware of antibody cross-reactivities. TTF1, which is usually used to determine a primary lung adenocarcinoma origin, may be expressed in 2.4 % of breast cancers \[ 12 \]. A panel of markers, including GATA3, is recommended \[ 13 \].

As primary invasive papillary carcinoma is rare in the breast, the finding of an invasive tumour with papillary architecture occurring in the breast warrants exclusion of papillary metastases from other organ sites. Apart from comparison with the morphology of the non-mammary primary tumour, the use of immunohistochemistry can be diagnostically helpful. It is important to be aware of cross-reactivities of antibodies. For instance, TTF1 can be rarely positive in primary breast carcinomas, and ER can be expressed by lung adenocarcinomas. A panel of markers, including GATA3, which is expressed in breast carcinoma, is helpful

【24】#### Encapsulated Papillary Carcinoma

【25】Encapsulated papillary carcinoma shows a rounded contour with a fibrous capsule of varying thickness, contrasting with invasive papillary carcinoma where papillary tumour permeates the breast tissue in an irregular manner.

【26】#### Invasive Micropapillary Carcinoma

【27】This invasive cancer shows morular, often centrally hollow, clusters of tumour cells residing within empty spaces. There is an inside-out pattern where luminal surfaces of epithelial cells face outwards into the stromal spaces, indicating reverse polarity. These micropapillary collections of tumour cells are devoid of investment by fibrovascular septa, unlike the invasive papillary carcinoma where invading papillary processes are accompanied by fibrovascular cores (Figs. 4.72 and 4.73 ). Immunohistochemistry for epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) and MUC-1 shows staining of the outer surfaces of the cells forming the morules (Fig. 4.74 ).

【72】Keywords

【73】Sclerosing adenosis Radial scar Complex sclerosing lesion

【74】Many different types of both benign and malignant breast lesions can be associated with stromal fibrosis and collagen deposition and can be broadly classified as sclerosing lesions \[ 1 – 3 \]. Recognising the aetiology of the fibrosis on excisional biopsy is usually not very difficult; however, extensive fibrosis and related histologic changes may create major diagnostic challenges on a limited sample such as a core needle biopsy. Sclerosing adenosis and radial scar/complex (radial) sclerosing lesion are two benign entities that will be described in this chapter. The main clinical significance of these lesions is that they may mimic invasive carcinoma clinically and radiographically as well as in gross and microscopic evaluations.

【75】Sclerosing Adenosis
-------------------

【76】### Definition

【77】Adenosis is defined as a relative increase in the number of acinar units in a terminal ductal lobular unit. Sclerosing adenosis refers to adenosis with extensive fibrosis that includes compression and distortion of acinar units \[ 4 \]. When proliferating glands expand lobular units significantly and form nodules or mass lesions, the terms nodular adenosis and adenosis tumour are used \[ 5 \].

【78】### Clinical Features

【79】Sclerosing adenosis is a frequent incidental microscopic finding in breast specimens removed for other indications. Sclerosing adenosis has been reported in 15–20 % of breast biopsies without carcinoma. It occurs in a wide age group but is most frequent in perimenopausal women. Regression of sclerosing adenosis has been noted in postmenopausal women. Most lesions are less than 2 cm and can be unifocal or multiple. The majority are associated with microcalcifications and/or architectural distortion that leads to biopsy. Therefore, screen detection in an asymptomatic patient is the most common mode of discovery. Less commonly, the presenting symptom may be a mass lesion on palpation or on imaging. Rarely, sclerosing adenosis may be associated with breast pain.

【80】### Imaging Features

【81】Sclerosing adenosis may present as microcalcifications, architectural distortion, or mass lesions (Fig. 5.1 ) \[ 6 \]. Microcalcifications are typically described as amorphous and clustered; pleomorphic and punctate microcalcifications can also be associated with sclerosing adenosis. This latter pattern cannot be differentiated from that of carcinoma, and biopsy is required for definitive diagnosis. Increased density with irregular margins with or without microcalcifications can also be a radiographic finding of sclerosing adenosis. This pattern closely mimics invasive carcinoma, especially tubular carcinoma. Mass-forming lesions are typically well circumscribed or lobulated. There are usually no significant MR findings. Twenty percent of cases of sclerosing adenosis may show intermediate enhancement.

【84】### Pathologic Features

【85】#### Macroscopic Pathology

【86】The gross appearance of sclerosing adenosis depends on the size and microscopic composition of the lesion. Since the majority of sclerosing adenosis lesions are small and have a combination of stromal and glandular components, they are imperceptible on macroscopic evaluation. If a lesion has extensive fibrosis, it may appear as white and vaguely nodular (Fig. 5.2 ). Lesions composed predominantly of glandular components with epithelial proliferation may appear as circumscribed, rubbery, pale tan nodules.

【89】#### Microscopic Pathology

【90】Sclerosing adenosis is characterised by enlarged lobular units due to nodular proliferation of ducts and acini that are compressed and distorted by stromal collagen (Figs. 5.3 , 5.4 , and 5.5 ) \[ 4 , 7 \]. The normal lobular appearance is distorted by fibrosis, particularly in the centre of the lesion, where distorted glands may have an angulated appearance and mimic invasive carcinoma (Fig. 5.6 ). However, the lobulocentric nature of the lesion, which is best appreciated on low magnification, is maintained and can be the most important histologic feature to differentiate it from invasive cancer (Fig. 5.6 ). The ducts have both luminal epithelial and peripheral myoepithelial cells. Although the presence of a dual cell population is easy to appreciate on haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) sections in most cases, confirmation by immunohistochemistry may be helpful in selective instances to illustrate the preservation of myoepithelial cells (Fig. 5.7 ). The ratio of epithelial and myoepithelial cells can vary significantly from case to case (Fig. 5.8 ).

【91】In some cases, there is significant epithelial atrophy and preferential proliferation of myoepithelial cells. In others, both epithelial and myoepithelial components appear hyperplastic. The basement membrane around glands of sclerosing adenosis is usually thickened and prominent. Occasionally, both epithelial and myoepithelial cells undergo metaplastic changes. Apocrine metaplasia of epithelium, spindle cell morphology, and myoid differentiation of myoepithelium are commonly seen in sclerosing adenosis. The term apocrine adenosis is used when the entire lesion of sclerosing adenosis shows apocrine metaplasia (Fig. 5.9 ) \[ 8 – 10 \]. Microcalcifications are a common microscopic feature of sclerosing adenosis and can be present either in fibrotic stroma or in ductal lumens. Atypical ductal and atypical lobular hyperplasia or in situ carcinoma may involve sclerosing adenosis. These may cause major diagnostic difficulties, especially on core needle biopsies. Involvement of sclerosing adenosis by ductal carcinoma in situ may mimic invasive carcinoma, and it is one of thecommonly mistaken diagnoses on core needle biopsies. Ductal carcinoma in situ involving sclerosing adenosis can be high grade and arise within sclerosing adenosis. The integrity of the individual acini and preservation of myoepithelium may be difficult to appreciate on H&E sections alone (Figs. 5.10 , 5.11 , and 5.12 ). Lobulocentric architecture of sclerosing adenosis versus infiltrative growth pattern of invasive carcinoma, a background of dense fibrotic stroma of sclerosing adenosis versus the more cellular (desmoplastic) stroma of invasive carcinoma, should be useful in arriving at the correct diagnosis. Using immunohistochemical stains to highlight myoepithelial cells will be helpful \[ 11 – 14 \].

【92】Perineural pseudoinvasion has been reported in 2 % of sclerosing adenosis cases (Fig. 5.13 ) \[ 15 \]. Sclerosing adenosis glands and ducts may be present around nerves, most commonly in the perineurium, but rarely in nerve fibres. The benign appearance of the glands and the preserved myoepithelial layer around the ducts will be helpful to differentiate these glands from invasive carcinoma.

【0】ttention testing to assess such patients. One should look for the ability to divide attention between different sensory sources (hearing and seeing targets) and for selective responding. We use the Testbatterie zur Aufmerksamkeitsprifung (TAP) (Zimmermann， 1992)， which provides subtests for divided and selective attention. In the divided attention task， a square built up by 4 × 4 points is shown. Small crosses cover seven or eight of the points. During the task these crosses jump irregu-larly to the different points and sometimes four of them are grouped like a small square (covering four adjacent points of the large square). The task is to press the button as soon as four crosses form a such square. At the same time participants hear high and low tones. They also must press the button as soon as two same tones are presented directly in a sequence. The duration of the task is between 4 and 5 minutes. The selective attention task is a variant of the Simon paradigm： the participant must press the left or the right button as soon as an arrow appears pointing in this direction. The arrows appear very shortly on the left and the right side of the screen， thus sometimes pro-ducing a conflict between the side where they are presented and the side where they point to. Accordingly， the test probes selective visuospatial atten-tion and response inhibition.**

【1】**Experienced deficits in attention are state marker for depression， and a lack of self-conscience in one’s own cognitive performance due to depressive mood can motivate the patients to attend a neuropsychological assessment. Subtle deficits in the divided attention have been demonstrated in patients suffering from depression and they seem not to recover even after remission from the mood disorder (Reppermund et al.， 2007； Reppermund， Ising， Lucae， & Zihl， 2009).**

【2】The copying task of the CERAD-NAB is much too easy for mild impair-ments in visuoconstructive functions. Therefore we use the Block design test

【3】**of the Wechsler Intelligence Examination in middle-aged patients. On the other hand， the block design test is hypersensitive for visuospatial perfor-mance and an impairment in this task should only be taken as indication to reproduce the deficit with additional tasks (e.g.， copying the Rey-Osterrieth complex figure) and with dorsal visuospatial subtests from the Visual Object and Perception Battery (compare the Chapter 3： The Alphasynucleinopathies：Parkinson’s Disease， Lewy Body Dementia， and Multisystem Atrophy， on alpha synucleinopathy on the meaning of these tests：for differential diagnosis).**

【4】**1.6 Structured and efficient testing presupposes a structured and efficient anamnesis**

【5】**The specific strategy of testing patients for a differential diagnosis should be based on a preliminary idea/suspicion of the patient’s disease (whereby this hypothesis should be reformulated if test results are discrepant). The anam-nesis provides the necessary information to formulate a first hypothesis for the testing strategy((Chapter 8：： A Short Guideline forthe Neuropsychological Differential Diagnosis of the Dementias， provides a guideline which information should be looked for after having formulated a first hypothesis for the diagnosis). For many patients， one will have to go back to the anamnesis more than once or patients and their relatives must be given questionnaires to validate the etiological hypothesis. An anamnesis should start with patients providing a description of their problems (by them-selves). It is important to ask relatives not to intervene during this phase and to wait with comments and additional information until the anamnesis of the patient is finished. After the spontaneous delineation of the problems， that is， the reasons for attending the neuropsychological assessment， the anamnesis should primarily focus on the functions of the autonomous nervous system. This includes problems with swallowing and speaking (hoarseness)， pro-blems with vertigo， incontinence and constipation， erectile dysfunctions， and any sleep issues (duration， depth， and motor unrest such as speaking during sleep， and restless legs). Disorders of the autonomous nervous system， in situations where they cannot be explained by additional diseases， are fre-quently anindicationforrtypicalOTatypical1Parkinson's disease. Incontinence might be a symptom of normal pressure hydrocephalus. Finally**

【6】**regularly sleeping 10 or more hours a daycan be aa sign of ongoing neurodegeneration.**

【7】**The anamnesis should then focus on walking impairments， experienced falls， and postural instability as well as the use of the hands， handwriting， and any existing tremor. Resting tremor， frequent falls， problems with pos-tural balance， and limited handwriting abilities are frequent problems in idio-pathic and atypical Parkinson’s disease. The third major topic of the anamnesis concerns the senses， that is， deficits in seeing， hearing， smelling， and taste. Hypoacusis (partial loss of hearing ability) is a common problem in elderly individuals which leads to social isolation and may have detrimen-tal effects on cognition. Therefore advising the patient to use hearing aids the whole day might be helpful. Olfactory deficits may be the first signs of a beginning Parkinson’s disease. Furthermore the patient should be asked about his or her appetite as well as possible weight loss since weight loss is common in patientsVwith dementia. In this case， weight lossis usually accompanied by some loss of appetite or of having a regular meal. A signifi-cant weight loss (>8 kg in less than half a year) without any explanation(e.g.， another disease， voluntary reduction of caloric intake) should be han-dled as a warning signal for a possible cancer or tumor growth.**

【8】**The next step of the anamnesis should focus on the cognitive functions of memory， working memory， attention， and language. Patients with subjective memory impairments should always be asked whether they have problems with orientation in new environments (e.g.， when they are on vacation). The anamnesis should also try to determine whether the subjective memory impairment concerns episodic memory (Can you remember things that you heard yesterday?) or working memory (Do you (only) forget what your intention is when you move into the next room?). Working memory pro-blems are uncommon in Alzheimer’s disease； however， patients often con-fuse them with episodic memory problems. To gain a better impression of the problem， one may also ask whether the patients usually remember the forgotten events through recognition， that is， after receiving some cues about the event by relatives or friends. Intact recognition but high forgetfulness biases the diagnostic hypothesis away from AD.**

【9】**Attentional performance should be assessed by differentiating between distractibility and tiredness. Again， excessive tiredness1LsSunusual for Alzheimer’s disease. Falling asleep during the day may be caused by sleep problems (e.g.， sleep apnea) or by cardiovascular diseases. Both are often associated with cognitive problems. If patients stress that they tire quickly， one should also ask if they experience mental slowing when confronted with problems. Mental slowing is a typical problem in patients with white matter lesions (vascular dementia) as well as in patients with Parkinson’s disease.**

【10】**The questions regarding language impairments concern understanding， word finding problems， and reduced drive for verbal communication. It is important to inquire about comprehension and word finding problems**

【11】**separately and to make sure that the patients report their verbal understand-ing abilities independent of hearing problems. If the patient reports word finding problems，oneshould examine (as with memory impairments) whether this impairment started suddenly， if it is slowly increasing or if it is constant. Another important question is whether it concerns the speaking or the access of the words. Moreover， it is important to look for paraphasia dur-ing the interaction with the patient. Paraphasia may concern the use of a wrong， but semantically related word or producing phonological similar but deviating words. It is important to note which of these possibilities are pres-ent. Another aspect of language is how the patient’s speech sounds： are there any signs of dysarthric speech or reduction in the force of the voice? If the patients are answering only in short sentences， one should also ask if they have lost interest in or reduced their amount of verbal interactions.**

【12】**The last topic of the anamnesis regarding subjectively experienced changes concerns mood. Questioning patients about mood changes should cover aspects such as depressed or euphoric mood， loss of drive， social with-drawal， increased irritability， anxiety and fearfulness， and being driven by unrest. Feeling more dependent on others is typical for patients with AD， whereas social withdrawal and increased irritability in the presence of stran-gers might be an indication of the behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia. On the other hand， increased short-term irritability and affect labil-ity are symptoms often associated with vascular dementia. If the patient tries to encourage a relative to answer the questions during the anamnesis， the development of the patient’s interpersonal dependency， for example， a recent aversion of being home alone， should be examined.**

【13】**The last part of the anamnesis concerns the medical history. The patient should be asked about any drugs or medications he or she is taking. The meaning of the question has also been introduced above. It is also important to ask if they have already experienced any neurological， psychiatric or psy-chological disorder， or disease during their life. This question should be broadened to include the medical history of the patient’s family as well. There are some kinds of dementia that have a strong genetic component(e.g.， behavioral frontotemporal lobe dementia， early onset Alzheimer’s dis-ease). Finally， whether the patient has been assessed by cranial Computer Tomography or Magnet Resonance Imaging should be established and the results should be requested.**

【14】**After having finished the anamnesis with the patients， the relatives should be asked whether the patient’s answers fit their impressions or whether there are differences. After discussing potential differences between the patients report and that of the relatives， one should explicitly ask whether the patients suffer from motor unrest during night-time dreaming (more specifically， whether there are any signs of a“REM sleep behavior disorder”， compare Chapter 3： The Alphasynucleinopathies： Parkinson’s Disease， Lewy Body Dementia， and Multisystem Atrophy， for this disorder)， how long they sleep**

【15】**during the day， whether there is a change in appetite and how the relatives rate the memory performance. Another important topic concerns the rela-tive’s impression of the patient’s mood and behavior. If there are signs of increased irritability and disinhibition， whether the patient is only aggressive at home or whether the patient is also aggressive and/or show aberrant behavior towards strangers should be determined. Relatives should also fill out questionnaires regarding the instrumental abilities of daily living， the neuropsychiatric inventory and whether the patient moves and speaks during sleep as well as a questionnaire concerning REM sleep behavior disorder. These questionnaires will be discussed later.**

【16】**1.7Summary： Prospect of neuropsychological testing of dementia**

【17】**As worldwide life expectancy raises， the upcoming decades will see a global increase in the number of patients with dementia. This will be accompanied by an enormous medical and psychosocial challenge for the patients， their relatives， and society. The diagnosis of dementia is a syndrome diagnosis and should therefore be based on accepted criteria (e.g.， the ICD-10). The syndrome of dementia can be caused by several diseases which must be dif-ferentiated. Only an etiological classification (e.g.， which is listed in ICD-10) permits a well-founded statement about disease progress and necessary treat-ment. Dementia is a clinical， descriptive diagnosis； it does not necessarily imply a prognostic statement and even if the cause is progressive neurode-generative the long-term course may vary considerably between patients.**

【18】**Effective treatment for dementia relies on precise and early diagnosis because in later stages the neurodegenerative process already caused irrevers-ible atrophy. During later phases of dementia， delaying its progression will be the most important concern. There are currently no specific or clear-cut biomarkers for many types of dementia. Therefore the differential diagnosis relies on the clinical investigation of the patients and on the combination of different information to arrive at the most appropriate diagnosis (“probable”in the case of a combined positive functional and somatic validation and“possible”in the case of only the functional impairments coinciding with the diagnosis). Neuropsychological testing is one method that can assist the dif-ferential diagnosis of dementia at the earliest clinical period of the disease. While screening tests like the MMSE help in determining the severity of the dementia， they do not provide information for a differential diagnosis， or do they detect the first signs of cognitive decline. Moreover， most of the screen-ing tests do not rely heavily enough on age-， gender-， and education-based test norms. Because these variables influence the results of screening tests， these tests do not convey reliable information. Rather， they provide only an estimation of the disease’s progression. Such a rating is important to judge the probable handicaps of the patient in everyday life and to assist the**

【19】**decision-making process regarding， for example， driving or nursing homes. Neuropsychological testing in patients with suspected dementia therefore has two purposes： predicting the ability to live independently and to offer infor-mation about the possible cause of the impairment (supporting a specific dif-ferential diagnosis). Hopefully in the near future， there will be a third purpose of neuropsychological testing： to inform patients about the best func-tional treatment as well as its optimal level of difficulty (the scarce literature concerning neuropsychological rehabilitation in the specific dementias will be discussed at the end of the following chapters).**

【20】With respect to the purpose of differential diagnosis， Table 1.14 provides an overview of a set of core tests that may be used for a first impression of the cognitive problems. These core tests should be complemented by further tests depending on the etiological hypothesis based on this assessment.

【21】**The CERAD-NAB is a standardized test battery that is based on the results of more than 1100 control subjects (Schmid et al.， 2014) and there-fore the use of the CERAD-NAB as a core set of tests is recommended. In theory， a performance below an absolute cut-off score should be indicative of the specific neurodegenerative disease the patient is suffering from. Unfortunately， there seems to be no absolute cut-off scores for any subtest of the CERAD-NAB concerning differential diagnosing.**

【22】**The statement of a possible diagnosis depends on the formulation of assumptions regarding the kind of disease that might be present. Such assumptions depend on the anamnesis， which should encompass questions concerning cognitive deficits as well as autonomous functioning， walking， control of the hands， mood， and previous relevant diseases of the patient and their relatives. Together with the results of the CERAD-NAB and the other tests from the core set， it should be possible to define specific impairment patterns that help to develop a hypothesis for the differential diagnosis. Presence of diffuse infiltrate， prominent lymphoepithelial lesions， extensive infiltration of muscularis mucosae， cyto-logic atypia of lymphoid cells， and Dutcher bodies in plasma cells favor MALT lymphoma over reactive process \[4，10，31\]. Presence of monotypic plasma cells， significant predomi-nance of B cells (CD20+) over T cells (CD3+)， and aberrant CD43 expression by B cells is also helpful in establishing the diagnosis of lymphoma. Presence of lymphoid follicles sur-rounded by small lymphocytes or marginal zone cells that colonize the epithelium and infiltrate diffusely lamina pro-pria is also suggestive of lymphoma \[24\]. In cases in which histologic and immunophenotypic findings are not conclu-sive， the diagnosis of an “atypical lymphoid infiltrate” is jus-tified， with the understanding that the patient will be followed with subsequent biopsy after treatment. Molecular testing for B-cell clonality is helpful， but rare cases of severe H. pylori-associated gastritis have been reported to yield monoclonal populations by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) \[46\].

【12】Grading systems for evaluation of lymphoid infiltrate in gastric biopsies have been proposed and are often used when communicating the morphologic results to gastroenter-ologists： negative (no gastritis) with scattered plasma cells in lamina propria and no lymphoid follicles (grade 0)； chronic active gastritis (clusters of lymphocytes within lamina propria but no lymphoepithelial lesions or follicles； grade 1)； chronic active gastritis with lymphoid follicles (prominent follicles _........1_ with mantle zone and plasma cells but no lymphoepithelial lesions； grade 2)； suspicious， probably reactive (follicles sur-rounded by lymphocytes that infiltrate lamina propria and occasional lymphoepithelial lesions； grade 3)； suspicious， probably lymphoma (follicles surrounded by lymphocytes with either a centrocyte morphology or a monocytoid appear-ance that diffusely infiltrate lamina propria and epithelium(grade 4)； and MALT lymphoma (grade 5) \[24，47，48\].

【13】Correlation with molecular analysis for B-cell clonal-ity (PCR) and/or fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) studies for t(11；18) may be needed in some cases to estab-lish the definite diagnosis. The t(11；18) is not present in reac-tive processes (even those preceding MALT lymphoma) and other low-grade lymphomas \[49\]. The PCR results have to be

【15】_Low-Grade B-Cell Lymphomas_

【16】Prominent colonization of reactive (residual) follicles may imitate FL. Careful evaluation of phenotypic markers， especially CD10 and BCL6， helps in the differential diag-nosis. FLs are positive for CD10 and BCL6； MCL can be distinguished from MZL by coexpression of CD5 and BCL1(cyclin D1) and SLL/CLL by coexpression of CD5 and CD23.

【17】_Plasmacytoma_

【18】**Occasional MZL in the GI tract (similar to other locations) may show an extensive plasmacytic differentiation， raising the possibility of plasma cell neoplasm (plasmacytoma). The presence of scattered B cells (or minute clonal B-cell popula-tion by flow cytometry)， the lack of the expression of BCL1， CD56， and CD117 by plasma cells， and the presence of other histologic features seen in MALT lymphomas (e.g.， lympho-epithelial lesions， reactive lymphoid follicles， and/or CD43expression by B cells) favor lymphoma. Plasmacytomas in the stomach are extremely rare.**

【19】_T-Cell Lymphomas_

【20】T-cell lymphomas are distinguished by immunophenotyping. Presence of very prominent colonization of the gastric epi-thelium by T cells， especially if they are negative for CD5， should raise the possibility of enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma (EATL).

【21】_Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma_

【22】Based on the WHO classification (2008)， the presence of solid or sheet-like proliferations of large cells indicates DLBCL(with or without accompanying MALT lymphoma) \[50\].

【23】**GASTRIC DLBCL**

【24】DLBCL of the stomach (Figure 46.7) may occur de novo or in the background of H. pylori infection and MALT lym-phoma \[34，51-53\]. Helicobacter pylori is identified in ~35%

【25】of gastric large B-cell lymphomas， more often when there is an accompanying low-grade component of MALT type(65% vs. 15%) \[34\]. Histologically， DLBCL of the stomach resemble its nodal counterpart with diffuse infiltrate of large cells with centroblastic， immunoblastic， or mixed cytomor-phology. Subset of cases shows rearrangement of BCL6(Figure 46.8). Majority of tumors are CD10-， BCL6+， and less often MUM1+. CD43 is often positive and occasional lym-phomas may be CD5+ (Figure 46.9). Aggressive large B-cell lymphomas with plasmablastic morphology and cytoplas-mic ALK expression have also been reported in the stomach(Figure 46.10) \[54\]. Plasmablastic large B-cell lymphomas are negative for CD45 and B-cell markers (CD19， CD20， and

【28】**Differential Diagnosis**

【29】**The diagnostic considerations include MALT lymphoma with large cell transformation， other high-grade lymphomas， BL， blastoid or pleomorphic variant of MCL， some T-cell lymphomas， extramedullary myeloid tumor (EMT)， mela-noma， and poorly differentiated carcinoma. Immunostaining(e.g.， cy tokeratins for carcinoma； S100 for melanoma； MPO， CD15， CD68， and CD117 for EMT； pan-T-cell markers for T-cell disorders) helps in the differential diagnosis.**

【30】**BURKITT LYMPHOMA**

【31】Extranodal involvement is common in patients with BL， and the abdomen (stomach， small and large intestines， genito-urinary tract) is the most frequent site followed by jaws and facial bones. GI tract lymphomas， including BL， often occur in patients with HTV infection. The published data showed that a high proportion of patients with gastric BL have a localized disease that is limited to stages l and 2， and that the localized BL has an outstanding outcome \[131. Figures 46.11and 46.12 present BL involving the stomach. Tumor cells are rather monomorphous， medium sized with scanty， often vacuolated cytoplasm. They are positive for B-cell markers， CD10， and BCL6， and do not express BCL2. Ki-67 index is very high (~100%).

【55】EMT (granulocytic sarcoma， myeloid sarcoma) rarely involves the GI tract (most often small intestine)， but stom-ach localization has been reported (Figure 46.19). 【57】**INTRODUCTION**

【58】**GI tract is one of the most common sites of extranodal lymphomas.Primary non-Hodgkin卜lymphomas(HLs) represent 3%-4% of all of the GI tract malignancies， and the most frequent types of lymphoma include MCL(large intestine > small intestine)， DLBCL； MZL (large intestine > small intestine)； FL (small intestine > large intestine)； EATL (small intestine> large intestine)； PTCL， unspecified (PTLU)； ALCL (small intestine>large intes-tine)； BL； B-CLL； and ENKTL.**

The median age is 56 years with male and female patients equally involved(although female predominance was reported in some series). In contrast to nodal disease， the majority of cases are detected in clinical stage I/II. 【6】**【病因】**

【7】**本病为常染色体隐性遗传。硫脂是少突胶质细胞、雪旺细胞的细胞膜上的正常成分、溶酶体 (lysosome) 中的芳香基硫酸酯酶 A (sulfatase A) 使硫脂分解成脑糖苷。在异染性脑白质营养不良的病人中，由于芳香基硫酸酯酶A的缺乏，导致了硫脂在少突胶质细胞膜和雪旺细胞膜上的异常沉积。这种强酸性的脂质引起髓鞘分子结构及髓鞘水合作用的改变而发病。硫脂在酸性尼氏染色下不呈紫蓝色而为棕色，故称其为异染性。**

【8】**【病理】**

【9】**大脑半球、脑干及小脑白质内广泛脱髓鞘改变，以少突胶质细胞脱髓鞘最明显，弓形纤维不受累。镜检可见异染色性类脂质小球散在于脑白质间和吞噬细胞、少突胶质细胞内。硫脂沉积也可累及齿状核与脑干核。**

【10】**【临床表现】**

【11】**主要临床表现为进行性痴呆和痉挛性瘫痪。根据起病年龄可分为以下三型：**

【12】**1.婴几晚期型 最常见。病儿出生后各方面常发育正常，自1~2岁时开始不能维持正常姿势，行走困难和动作笨拙，肌张力下降，运动减少，以后智力减退，由软瘫转为硬瘫，并可出现小脑共济失调、眼震、视神经萎缩、失语，逐渐为去脑强直、痴呆。多于5岁前死于继发性感染或中枢性高热。**

【13】**2.少年型于4~5岁起病，多以视力和听力障碍或学习成绩下降为首发症状，进展缓慢，以后出现共济失调和痉挛性瘫痪。**

【14】**3.成年型 最初常表现为精神方面的改变，可误诊为精神分裂症。随着病情的发展，逐渐出现进行性痴呆和痉挛性瘫痪。**

【21】**(高培毅 林 燕)**

【22】**第二节 肾上腺性脑白质营养不良**

【23】**肾上腺性脑白质营养不良 (adrenoleukodystrophy， ALD) 又称性连锁遗传谢尔德病·(sex-linked schilder's disease) 和肾上腺弥漫性轴周性脑炎等。本病为性连锁隐性遗传所致过氧化体内乙酰辅酶A合成酶缺陷引起的遗传代谢性病变，多发生于3-15岁男孩；少数病人为常染色体隐性遗传，成年人发病。**

【24】**【病因】**

【25】**由于组织细胞内过氧化体缺乏乙酰辅酶A合成酶，致使胆固醇脂或脂肪酸合成异常，而导致饱和极长链脂肪酸在组织中异常聚集，引起脑白质脱髓鞘和肾上腺功能低下。正常时，乙酰辅酶A对饱和极长链脂肪酸进行β氧化，使之成为短链脂肪酸。 ALD病人血浆饱和极长链脂肪酸含量异常增高是由于体内缺乏乙酰辅酶A合成酶，故不能及时切断极长链脂肪酸成为短链脂肪酸所致。**

【26】**【病理】**

【27】**主要表现为大脑白质广泛性、对称性脱髓鞘改变。脑白质脱髓鞘改变先从大脑白质后部开始，由后向前、由中心向外周蔓延，累及枕叶、顶叶和颞叶，额叶通常不受影响。病灶也可穿过胼胝体压部使两侧病灶连成一片，围绕在双侧侧脑室体后部周围。病灶最外周是髓鞘正在破坏的区域，仅有髓鞘脱失和轴索稀疏；病灶逐渐向内呈炎性反应区，除了明显的脱髓鞘改变外，还可见血管周围炎性细胞和血脑屏障的破坏；中心部的陈旧性病灶为胶质增生，并可有钙质沉积。病程后期在皮质脊髓束可以发生华勒变性(Wallerian degeneration)。光镜下可以见到髓鞘崩解区有大量格子细胞。电镜下，巨噬细胞、胶质细胞内有特异性的脂质板层，为饱和极长链脂肪酸积聚。晚期，由于脑白质广泛减少可造成脑皮质萎缩、脑室扩大。可同时存在肾上腺萎缩。**

【28】**【临床表现】**

【29】**本病呈进行性发展，无缓解期，预后差。根据发病年龄及损害部位不同分为两种类型：**

【30】**1.儿童型 最常见，仅见于男性，通常在3~15岁发病。表现为行为改变、智力减退、视力下降、听力下降、小脑共济失调、四肢痉挛性瘫痪等。晚期有肾上腺皮层功能不全症状(异常皮肤色素沉着)，乃至危象。病程进行性发展，多在发病后几年内死亡。**

【31】**_2\._ .成人型 少见，为常染色体隐性遗传，是肾上腺性脑白质营养不良的变异型，又称肾上腺脊髓神经病和肾上腺脑白质脊髓神经病。此型见于20~30岁男性，病程**

【32】**长，有智力减退、肾上腺皮质功能不全、小脑性共济失调和四肢痉挛性瘫痪等。**

【34】**病程早期首先在顶、枕叶白质出现病灶，以后逐渐向前发展并累及颞叶白质，也可经胼胝体压部使两侧病灶融合而表现为内“蝴蝶”状。ALD 典型 MRI 表现为双侧侧脑室三角区旁的枕，顶叶白质区对称性、“蝴蝶”样异常信号影，病灶边缘不规则(图12-2)。T加权像上，病灶表现为低信号影，无占位征象。侧脑室体后部及三角区可有轻度扩大。T加权像时病灶显示为高信号影。静脉注人对比剂后，在病灶的外周下层的炎性反应区可有线条样增强影。**

【40】**第三节 球影细胞脑白质世养不良**

【41】**球形细胞脑白质营养不良 (globoid cell leukodystrophy)是一常染色体隐性遗传疾病，婴儿期出现症状，病程较短，，一般不超过3年。本病又称为 Krabbe 病或半乳糖脑苷脂沉积症。**

【42】**【病因】**

【43】**由于溶酶体异常致使B-半乳糖苷酶缺乏导致脑苷酯类代谢障碍而使髓鞘形成不良。**

【44】**【病理】**

【45】**为大脑、小脑和脑干白质广泛、对称性的髓鞘形成不良及脑白质变性、萎缩，皮层下弓状纤维显示正常。病变区少突胶质细胞数目减少，脱髓鞘广泛，最后导致胶质细胞及纤维明显增生。本病最特征性改变为在病变区白质内小血管周围有成群的类球形细胞以及巨噬细胞聚集。这种类球形细胞呈圆形， PAS 染色为强阳性，胞浆常为嗜碱性，胞浆内含有大量髓鞘的重要成分-半乳糖苷脂。基底节灰质受累较常见，脑**

【46】**皮质多变薄。**

【47】**【临床表现】**

【48】**有家族遗传史，首发症状早于异染性脑白质营养不良患儿，常见于生后3~5个月内起病。病前常有发热，热退后开始出现症状。最早的临床表现为由于脱髓鞘性多神经病引起的深腱反射减弱的锥体束异常，四肢出现痉挛状态。检查可见头小、发育迟缓、智力下降、痴呆、视神经萎缩、皮质盲、四肢痉挛性瘫痪。脑脊液检查可有轻度淋巴细胞增多，蛋白总量、白蛋白和α球蛋白增高，y-球蛋白降低。一般在3年内死亡。**

【49】**【MRI征象}**

【50】**早期在双侧侧脑室周围脑白质区及半卵圆中心出现对称性片状异常信号影，病灶边缘模糊。T加权像显示为低信号影，T，加权像则表现为高信号景，丘脑、尾状核可呈对称性高信号影。内囊及胼胝体髓鞘形成不良，显示为体积变小。晚期为弥漫性脑白质萎缩。**

【51】**{高培毅** **林** **燕)**

【52】**第四节 海绵大脑白质营养不良**

【53】**海绵状脑白质营养不良 (spongiform leukodystrophy)又称 Canavan 病、Van Bo·gaetrt 病、海绵样变性(spongy degeneration) 和脑白质海绵状硬化症等。是一种较罕见的家族遗传性疾病，呈常染色体隐性遗传。**

【54】**【病因】**

【55】**由于线粒体异常致使乙酰天门冬酰基酶每(N-acetylaspartoacylase) 缺乏导致质子膜通透性异常而发病。**

【56】**【病理】**

【57】**为严重的脑水肿，脑重量和体积增加。脑水肿以皮层深层和白质浅层受累为主，中央白质区相对较轻。随着病情的进展逐步累及基底节、小脑、脑干和脊髓。镜下见病变区广泛的空泡形成，而造成大脑白质的海绵状变性。皮层深层的空泡常见于神经元和小血管周围，由原浆型星性细胞高度肿胀所致；白质浅层的空泡位于细胞外区和髓鞘板层内。晚期可有继发脱髓鞘和胶质增生。**

【58】**【临床表现】**

【59】**本病临床表现主要为中枢神经系统体征和巨颅。患儿出生时正常，多在生后3个月内起病。最初出现呕吐、哺乳困难，伴惊厥发作。以后逐渐出现肢体松弛，颈肌力弱、举头困难，渐至肌张力增高，去大脑强直与抽搐发作，视神经萎缩及尖明。本病**

【60】**第十二章 脑变性和脑白质病**

【61】**的特点之一是头围快速增大。常在5岁前死亡。个别患儿起病较晚，大约5岁以后发病，以智力低下为主，可有小脑性共济失调、视力障碍和视神经萎缩等。**

【62】**【MRI征象】**

【63】**大脑半球皮层下、白质区广泛性、对称性异常长T、长T：信号影。双侧基底节、丘脑、脑干和小脑可显示正常或轻度异常。三脑室和双侧侧脑室可见明显扩大，中线结构无移位。病孩头颅巨大，颅缝分离。静脉注入对比剂后病变区无增强。晚期表现为脑萎缩及脑室扩大。**

【66】**第五节 淀泥性皮质外轴蒙再生障断症**

【67】**先天性皮质外轴索再生障碍症又称佩-梅氏病((Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease， PMD)、慢性婴儿型脑硬化和家族性脑中叶硬化病等。是一种较罕见的家族遗传性疾病，呈伴性隐性遗传或常染色体隐性遗传。**

【68】**【病因】**

【69】**本病为髓磷脂形成缺陷而使髓鞘发育不全所致。**

【70】**【病理】**

【71】**大脑半球深、浅白质呈广泛性、弥漫性发育不全的髓鞘斑片状脱失，蛋白脂质明显减少，髓鞘脱失区中遗留有髓鞘比较完整的孤岛，间杂以颗粒状的嗜苏丹物质。病变可累及小脑及脊髓。晚期病灶内有神经胶质增生，形成硬化。**

【72】**【临床表现】**

【73】**PMD分为两型，即婴儿型(Ⅰ型))和新生儿型(Ⅱ型)。婴儿型(Ⅰ型)为伴性隐性遗传，见于男孩，病情进展缓慢，可持续多年。新生儿型(Ⅱ型)为伴性隐性遗传或常染色体隐性遗传，病情发展迅速，男孩多见，但偶尔也发生于女性。两种类型的临床表现大致相同，只是起病时间和病情进展的快慢有所不同。典型表现为旋转性眼球震颤、头部抖动、小脑共济失调。多数病例在成年前死亡。**

【78】**巨脑性婴儿脑白质营养不良又称亚历山大 (Alexander)病、类纤维蛋白型脑白质营养不良 (fibrinoid leukodystrophy)。男孩多见。**

【80】**病因及遗传方式目前尚不十分清楚。**

【81】**【病理】**

【82】**可见脑体积和重量增加。病程早期，病变主要累及双侧额叶白质。以后逐渐累及基底节、丘脑和丘脑下部。肿胀退变的星形细胞内、血管周围间隙和室管膜下可见玻璃样嗜酸性纤维 (rosenthal纤维)沉积，同时伴有不同程度脱髓鞘改变。**

【99】**【临床表现】**

【100】**20~40岁间发病，女性多于男性。病程多为慢性，数年内可有多次发作加重及缓解过程。**

【101】**1..根据病程可分为**

【102】**(1)缓解复发型：约占70%，发病后可完全缓解，临床稳定数月至数年，2次或2次以上发作；**

【103】**(2)慢性进展型：约占10%，病情逐渐加重，无缓解期；**

【104】**(3)良性型：大约占10%-15%左右，一生仅有一次发作，以后几乎完全缓解；**

【105】**(4)恶性型：起病急，发展快，数月内死亡。**

【106】**2.根据损害部位及症状可分为**

【107】**(1)脊髓型；下肢感觉异常、排尿困难和痉挛性瘫等；**

【108】**(2)脑干/小脑型；颅神经症状、视力障碍、共济失调和眼球震颤等；**

【109】**(3)大脑型：偏瘫、半身感觉障碍和精神症状等。**

【110】**MRI征象】**

【111】**大脑半球内 MS 典型 MRI 表现为脑室旁白质区多发、散在椭圆形长T、长T异信号影，病灶大小多在3~5mm左右，病变边缘略显模糊(图12-3)。MS椭圆形斑块的长轴有与侧脑室壁成直角的倾向，胼胝体常受累，此两点可与脑缺血灶鉴别。新旧病灶可同时存在，但静脉注入对比剂后仅可见新鲜、活动期病灶增强。病程较长者胼胝体多见萎缩，矢状面见胼胝体体积缩小，边缘凹凸不平。脊髓型 MS 病灶多位于颈段和上胸段，横断面见 MS斑块常位于脊髓的侧后部，表现为长T、长T异常信号影。矢状面见病灶长度多在一个椎体长度左右。**

【112】**不典型 MS病灶可单发，病灶形似肿瘤。**

【113】**(高培毅** **林** **燕)**

【114】**第八节 皮层下动脉硬化性脑病**

【115】**皮层下动脉硬化性脑病 (subcortical arteriosclerotic encephalopathy， SAE) 又称为Binswanger病，是脑血管病的一种特殊类型。**

【116】**【病因】**

【117】**本病是由于脑深部小穿通突动脉硬化所引起大脑白质、基底节、小脑白质和桥脑等部位多灶性小动脉梗塞。**

【118】**第十二章 脑变性和脑白质病**

【119】**【病理】**

【120】**本病的主要病理表现为脑深部基底节、内囊、放射冠、桥脑以及小脑白质等处广泛性小动脉硬化以及动脉壁的透明样变，小动脉闭塞并引起微小软化灶。白质区有弥漫性轴索髓鞘脱失，脑室周围有多发性软化灶，同时可伴有大量胶质细胞增生。脑白质的损害主要集中在脑室周围的小动脉末梢边缘区域。多数病人可有脑室扩大。**

【121】**a.横断面T 加权像， b.Ti加权像见双侧脑室体部脑白质多发斑块状长T、长T信号影，边缘模糊，病灶可见融合**

【122】**\[临床表现】**

【123】**主要临床表现为痴呆、假性球麻痹、锥束和锥体外系损害等症状。**

【124】**【MRI征象】**

【125】**MRI表现T加权像见双侧侧脑室旁白质区较对称性稍低信号影，病变边缘模糊(图12-4)。基底节或内囊等处可伴有腔隙性梗塞灶。桥脑基底部也常可见斑片状稍低信号影。T：加权像时，病变表现为稍高信号影，边缘模糊，信号欠均匀。**

【126】**(高培毅 林 燕)**

【127】**第九节 进行性多灶性白质脑病**

【128】**进行性多灶性白质脑病 (progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy， PML) 是一由于机体细胞免疫功能损害导致潜伏感染的JC多瘤病毒再活化所引起的脱髓鞘病变。**

【129】**【病因】**

【130】**正常人体中存在属 DNA乳多空病毒组中的JC多瘤病毒。青春期，70%的人血清呈阳性。当机体由于某种原因免疫功能下降时发病。**

【131】**【病理】**

【132】**本病的主要病理改变为脑白质限局性脱髓鞘改变。镜下可见髓磷脂变灰，肿大的少突胶质细胞内含有充满了病毒颗粒的包涵体和星形细胞增生等变化。变形的少突胶质细胞多聚集在脱髓鞘区域的边缘。血管周围无炎性反应。(额叶及顶枕叶交界处皮层下白质区脱髓鞘改变最常见，以后逐渐波及深部白质、胼胝体、基底节和丘脑，偶可累及小脑、脑干及脊髓。灰质一般不受影响。**

【133】**【临床表现】**

【134】**PML 多发生在免疫功能低下的病人，如淋巴瘤、白血病、AIDS病、先天性免疫缺陷综合征、器宫移植、系统性红斑狼疮、结核、结节病和非热带性口腔性腹泻等病的患者。临床上多表现为慢性、进行性精神异常、感觉功能障碍、视力损害、瘫痪和共济失调等，多于6~9个月内死亡。目前尚无有效治疗方法。**

【135】**【MRI征象】**

【136】**由于髓磷脂减少和水分增高， PML在 MRI影像上表现为额叶和顶枕叶交界处皮质下白质内单发或多发非对称性异常信号强度影，无占位征象(图12-5)。T加权像上，病变表现为低或等信号强度影；T加权像为高信号强度。静脉注射对比剂后病变通常不增强，病灶边缘增强少见。病程早期，病灶多呈斑片状、圆形或卵圆形。病灶信号呈均匀性，边界较清楚，主要位于皮层下白质浅层，使灰-白质交界向深部突出。晚期可见病灶融合或形成空腔。**

【137】**PML病灶多位于皮层下白质区，胼胝体受累较轻，此点与MS病灶常位于脑室**

【138】**第十二章 脑变性和脑白质病**

【139】**图12-5 进行性多灶性白质脑病**

【140】**a.横断面T加权像， b，T：加权像见右颗及左枕皮层下不规则形长T、长Tz异常信号影，病灶边缘略显模糊**

【141】**旁白质有所不同。**

【142】**(高培毅 林 燕)**

【143】**第十节 多发性脑根视性痴米**

【144】**多发性脑梗塞痴呆(multiple-infarct dementia) 又称血管性痴呆R (vascular demen-tia，VD)。**

【145】**【病因】**

【146】**多由于脑内 500gm 以下细小动脉硬化使脑血循环障碍引起全脑或局部脑组织缺血所致。**

【147】**【病理】**

【148】**(多发性脑梗塞最常见于基底节区、丘脑和侧脑室旁白质区。镜下见病灶新旧不一，有的则表现为神经组织缺血改变、脱髓鞘、胶质细胞增生；有的表现为神经细胞数量减少、组织结构疏松。**

【149】**【临床表现】**

【150】**多发性脑梗塞痴呆多见于60岁以上年龄段，无性别差异。病人常有高血压、冠**

【151】**心病或糖尿病史，以及一次或多次中风史。早期表现为记忆力下降、注意力不集中。以后逐渐出现定向力障碍、计算力障碍等。**

【152】**【MRI征象】**

【153】**图12-6 多发性脑梗塞性痴呆**

【154】**a、b.横断面T：加权像见双侧脑室旁多发散在、斑块样异常信号影**

【155】**(双侧基底节、丘脑及侧脑室旁多发、非对称性长T和长T异常缺血及软化灶(图12-6)。病灶新旧程度不一，边缘模糊多为较新的病灶；陈旧性病灶则边缘清晰。常常伴有脑萎缩改变。**

【156】**(高培毅 林 燕)**

【157】**第十一节 弥浚性硬化**

【158】**弥漫性硬化 (diffuse sclerosis) 是一种罕见的脱髓鞘疾病。又称 Schilder 病和弥漫性轴周性脑炎。本病常见于儿童，病理改变与多发性硬化相似，故多数学者认为是发生于儿童的一种多发性硬化的变异型。**

【159】**病因\]**

【160】**有学者报道本病为酶缺陷所致。散发者多有家族性。**

【161】**【病理】**

【162】**为大脑半球自室管膜下至皮层下白质广泛性脱髓鞘，呈弥漫不对称分布，常为一**

【163】**第十二章 脑变性和脑白质病**

【164】**侧较明显。皮层下弓形纤维常不受累。病灶内有轴索和髓鞘消失、血管周围格子细胞弥漫存在，星形细胞增生等改变。病变有从后向前，从上向下发展的倾向多由枕叶开始，逐渐蔓延至顶叶、颞叶与额叶或向对侧扩展，白质髓鞘脱失由深至浅融合成片。随着病程的发展，脑干、脊髓亦可受累。晚期多出现脑室扩大、脑池和脑沟增宽等脑萎缩表现。**

【165】**【临床表现】**

【166】**多见10岁前儿童，亚急性起病，进行性发展，无明显缓解期。临床上以精神症 _一一_ 状为主，伴锥体束征和皮质盲等。**

【167】**【MRI征象】**

【168】**大脑半球白质内出现广泛性不对称性的长T、长T，异常信号影，并以侧脑室周围最常见。静脉注入对比剂后无增强。可有脑萎缩表现。**

【169】**(高培毅 林 燕)**

【170】**第十二节 皮质-纹状体-脊链性**

【171】**皮质-纹状体-脊髓变性(cortico-striato-spinal degeneration) 又称 Creutzfeldt-Jakob病 (creutzfeldt-jakob disease， CJD)， 是一种以进行性痴呆为特征的疾病。**

【172】**【病因】**

【173】**目前多数学者认为本病系病毒感染所致。**

【174】**【病理】**

【175】**主要以脑皮质的弥漫性萎缩为特征，白质可受累。镜下见大脑、小脑、丘脑、基底节和脊髓的神经细胞消失，神经组织空泡化和胶质增生。病变区无炎性细胞浸润。脑组织的空泡化类似海绵样，故又将本病称为亚急性海绵状脑病。**

【176】**【临床表现】**

【177】**好发于中老年人，男女间无明显差异。主要临床表现为进展迅速的精神障碍和痴呆。**

【178】**【MRI征象】**

【179】**MRl影像无特征性，主要表现为广泛性脑沟、裂和蛛网膜下腔增宽，脑室扩大等脑萎缩征象。**

【180】**(高培毅** **林** **燕)**

【181】**第十三节 阿尔茨海默病**

【182】**阿尔茨海默病(alzheiner disease， AD)又称弥漫性大脑萎缩，是大脑皮层的一**

【183】**种变性病。**

【184】**【病因】**

【185】**AD的发病机制尚不完全清楚，目前有遗传缺陷、病毒感染、免疫异常和中毒等学说。**

【186】**【病理】**

【187】**主要表现为大脑皮层弥漫性萎缩，以颞叶和额叶最明显。镜下见神经细胞消失、白质变性，伴大量的老年斑 (senile plaque)、神经细胞缠结(neurofibrillary tangle)和颗粒空泡变性等。这些改变在海马部最为明显。**

【188】**【临床表现】**

【189】**通常缓慢起病，主要表现为记忆力下降、认知障碍、言语障碍、人格和行为改变。病变晚期出现痴呆、神经功能缺陷。预后差，多在病后数年死亡。**

【190】**MRI征象】**

【191】**MRI 检查见弥漫性脑萎缩，特别是颞叶萎缩最明显，表现为双侧侧脑室颞角扩大、环池和脉络裂增宽等(图12-7)。**

【195】**第十四节 _皮_ 宽 _病_**

【196】**皮克病 (pick disease)是引起老年性痴呆的一种疾病，临床上较少见。**

【197】**【病因】**

【198】**病因不明。**

【199】**【病理】**

【200】**病理上主要显示双侧额叶及颞叶前部脑萎缩改变。顶、枕叶通常不受累。镜下见病变区神经细胞消失、基质疏松、皮层下胶质增生及 Pick 小体。**

【201】**【临床表现】**

【202】**多见于 40~60岁年龄段，女性多于男性。主要以智力下降、注意力不集中、记忆力减退为首发症状，病情继续发展，晚期出现痴呆。**

【203】**【MRI征象】**

【204】**MRI表现为双侧额叶和颞叶脑沟、侧裂池增宽，侧脑室额角及颞角扩大。脑实质内一般无异常。**

【205】**(高培毅** **材** **燕)**

【206】**第十五节 息性播散性脑脊髓夹**

【207】**急性播散性脑脊髓炎(acute disseminated encephalomyelitis， ADEM) 是一组广泛累及脑和脊髓的急性炎性脱髓鞘性病变。**

【208】**【病因\]**

【209】**病因不清。由于本病常发生于病毒/细菌感染后(如麻疹、风疹、天花、水痘、腮腺炎、百日咳、流感和腥红热等)或发生于接种疫苗(如狂犬病、牛痘)之后，故认为是一种自身免疫性疾病。根据致病原因可以将 ADEM 分为感染后脑脊髓炎(postinfections encephalomyelitis)、疫苗接种后脑脊髓炎 (postvaccinal encephalomyeli-tis)和特发性脑脊髓炎。目前，特发性脑脊髓炎发病率有上升的趋势。**

【210】**病理】**

【211】**本病的病理表现以大脑、小脑、脑干和脊髓的白质中小静脉周围区域炎性细胞浸润、充血、水肿、髓鞘肿胀、断裂及脱失为特征，病变区常有点状坏死灶，并可融合为大片软化区。可有胶质细胞增生。病灶主要位于白质，但也可累及灰质及脊神经根。当脑白质内坏死和出血明显时，则称为急性出血性白质脑炎(Acute hemorrhagic lenkoencephalitis， AHL)。**

【212】**【临床表现】**

【213】**多见于儿童及青壮年，急性起病。发病前1个月内常有感染或接种史。多以头痛、全身无力、肌痛和恶心、呕吐为首发症状，体温可再度升高。随即中枢神经系统广泛受损，出现大脑、小脑、脑干及脊髓症状与体征。**

【217】**第十二章 脑变性和脑白质病**

【218】**【MRI征象】**

【219】**急性期 MRI 平扫可见双侧皮层下白质呈弥散对称性长工、长T2异常信号强度影，以双侧侧脑室周围白质区最明显。脑室可以因水肿而受压变小。静脉注入对比剂后偶见散在、斑片样轻度增强(图12-8)。随着病情的发展，双侧侧脑室周围白质异常信号区可以融合并累及灰质。当病变区内有出血时，可见散在、多发短T异常信号影。**

【220】**(高培毅 林 _燕)_**

【221】**第十六节 折豆状妆资性**

【222】**肝豆状核变性 (hepatolenticular degeneration， Hll)又称威尔逊病 (Wilson dis-ease)，是一种少见的常染色体隐性遗传性疾病。**

【223】**【病因】**

【224】**本病是由于铜转运和代谢异常，使铜在肝脏、豆状核、角膜和肾脏等组织和器官内异常沉积所致。实验室检查可见血清铜蓝蛋白、血清总铜量降低以及血清游离铜和尿铜排泄量增加。铜在体内特定部位异常沉积的机制迄今尚不十分清楚，肝胆排铜量减少、肠道吸收铜量过多，以及铜氧化酶这一异常蛋白对铜的吸引力等诸多因素均可存在。**

【225】**【病理】**

【226】**铜代谢异常使铜首先沉积于肝脏，在病变早期仅超微结构显示肝细胞内有线粒体异常，因此早期诊断比较困难。临床上由于出现肝大和黄疸肝细胞损害症状，故多误诊为肝炎。邹丽萍等报道的一组80例病例中，早期误诊率高达65%左右。晚期可出现肝硬化、脾脏肿大、腹水和食管静脉曲张等。**

【227】**脑内铜异常沉积的部位多见于基底节，其次为丘脑、脑干和齿状核。病变位于基底节时，又以壳核最为多见。锅异常沉积引起的脑内病灶往往是对称性的，但是两侧病变损害程度可有所不同。肝豆状核变性的脑磁共振影像信号表现与同异常沉积引起的脑组织病理改变和物理改变有关。铜在脑组织中的异常沉积较多的聚积在基底节、丘脑、脑干和齿状核等处的血管周围，(引起局部脑组织水肿、神经细胞变性或减少、脱髓鞘改变、胶质细胞(特别是星形细胞)增多。随着病情的发展，神经细胞可以出现坏死或囊变的小空腔，呈灶性海绵状空泡变性。上述脑组织的一系列病理变化均可以造成局部水成份的增多。**

【228】**【临床表现】**

【229】**儿童期或青春期发病，有家族史者约占1/3。随着铜在肝内饱和并释放、血清游**

【230】**离铜的明显增加，游离铜沉积在脑、角膜和肾脏等组织和器官。铜沉积于肾脏可以引起肾小管变性。当铜沉积于角膜缘时，临床检查可见在角膜缘有一黄棕色 Kayser-Fleischer 环(K-F环)。K-F环的出现是临床诊断肝豆状核变性的主要依据之一。**

【231】**游离铜在脑内沉积引起中枢神经系统损害多表现为震颤、肌张力增高等锥体外系症状和精神症状。**

【232】**【MRI征象】**

【233】**此时T加权像检查，病变部位多表现为低信号或稍低信号影；质子密度像和T2加权像则可表现为高信号影、低信号影或混杂信号影(图12-9)。磁共振检查时病灶呈现出长T和长T信号强度影反映了脑组织的病理变化。值得注意的是，当脑组织仅仅出现细胞内水肿时，由于水变化一般少于3%，故T加权像、质子密度像和Tz加权像检查多无异常信号影。这也是为什么一些作者在研究信号异常与临床表现之间的关系时多认为二者之间没有肯定的关系。随着细胞外水肿、脱髓鞘改变和神经细胞坏死或囊变等的出现，其弛豫时间延长，从而出现长T和长T信号影。当铜在脑组织中沉积量逐渐增多(病变部位铁的沉积量也随之增多)，这些重金属可以在局部造成磁力线扭曲而形成磁场梯度，在磁共振成像时造成局部去相位、信号丢失。此时的磁共振图像上，病灶表现为长T、短T信号强度影。有时，局部磁场梯度和脑组织**

【249】**【临床表现】**

【250】**最常见于17~30岁之间发病，临床表现为进行性小脑性共济失调、头部震颤、语言不利、锥体外系症状和脑干颅神经核损害症状。**

【254】**第十八节 遗传性小脑性共济状调**

【255】**脑性共济失调(hereditary cerebellar ataxia) 又称 Marie 共济失调，目前多数人将其称为遗传性痉挛性共济失调周(hereditary spastic ataxia)。**

【256】**【病因】**

【257】**病因不明，多数学者认为本病为常染色体显性遗传。**

【258】**【病理】**

【259】**病变主要位于小脑，并可侵及杨脑、延髓、脊髓和视神经。镜下见小脑浦肯野细胞大部分消失、轴索变性、白质脱髓鞘和胶质增生等。**

【260】**【临床表现】**

【261】**中青年发病，起病隐袭，通常表现为下肢无力、步态不稳、双手笨拙、讲话含糊，部分病人可有痉挛步态。**

【262】**【MRI 征象】**

【263】**MRI 检查可见小脑半球和小脑蚓部不同程度的萎缩性改变，表现为脑沟增宽、邻近蛛网膜下腔和脑室增宽。小脑萎缩的程度与病情的严重程度无明显关系。**

【264】**(高培毅** **林** **燕)**

【265】**第十九节 桥庙中央髓鞘溶解症**

【266】**桥脑中央髓鞘溶解症 (central pontine myelinolysis， CPM) 是一少见而又致命的、以桥脑髓鞘溶解为特征的病变。**

【267】**【病因】**

【268】**CPM的发病机制仍不十分清楚，但多数作者认为与血液中钠离子的浓度有关。当有低血钠时，快速纠正低血钠是 CPM 的主要原因。 Schmidt JA 等报道酗酒患者出现低血钠时，即使纠正钠的速度很快，也可出现 CPM， 因此认为酗酒是 CPM的诱**

【269】**第十二章 脑变性和脑白质病**

【270】**因。急性酒精摄人过多引起的低血钠也可导致 CPM。**

【271】**【病理】**

【272】**髓鞘溶解于桥脑基底的中央部开始，呈离心性扩散，常呈对称性分布，其病理特点为病变部位髓鞘脱失而无炎性改变，故命名为桥脑中央髓鞘溶解症。病灶占据桥脑基底的中心部分，受累区域内的髓鞘均被破坏，包括皮质脊髓束、皮质延髓束和皮质桥脑束。与破坏的髓鞘相反，轴索、神经细胞和血管结构都相对保留完好，病灶周围没有炎性细胞。以后又有作者发现除桥脑外，其它部位也可出现相同的病理改变，如内囊、丘脑、基底节、胼胝体及半卵圆中心，并将其称之为桥脑外髓鞘溶解症(ex-tral pontine myelinolysis， EPM)。**

【273】**【临床表现】**

【274】**CPM的临床表现与桥脑梗塞相似，临床上很难将二者区分开。典型病例为中年嗜酒者。此外，也可发生于患恶性肿瘤、慢性肺部疾患或慢性肾功能衰竭者。病人多表现为严重的代谢障碍，颅神经麻痹及长束征。病程进展很快，存活率低。**

【275】**【MRI征象】**

【276】**CPM 的 MRI影像学表现与其病理改变相符。CPM病灶位于桥脑基底的中央部分，病灶前方及侧方仅存一薄层脑组织未受累，病灶后缘可延伸至被盖的腹侧。桥脑最下部及中脑常不受累。因而在MRI横断面图像上病灶形态为圆形或蝴蝶形，矢状**

【282】**第二十节 系统性红斑狼滤**

【283】**系统性红斑狼疮 (systemic lupus erythematosus， SLE) 是一种自身免疫性疾病。**

【284】**\[病因】**

【285】**病因目前尚不十分清楚，可能为免疫复合体和病原抗体的沉积致使组织和细胞损害。本病主要侵犯全身胶原组织和血管，多累及皮肤、肾、肝、脾、肺和小血管，大约30%的病人可波及脑和脊髓的小血管。一般讲，脑、脑膜和脊髓的任何部分都可以受累。**

【286】**【病理】**

【287】**中枢神经系统的病理改变主要是脑膜增厚和脑实质小动脉、毛细血管和小静脉的弥散性炎性改变。受累的血管壁有玻璃样变性及纤维样渗出物，随后出现血管壁外层淋巴细胞浸润和纤维化，血管内膜增厚及血栓形成。由于管腔为血块、纤维样组织、血小板形成的血栓所阻塞，常导致脑组织的微小梗塞或继发性出血。**

【288】**【临床表现】**

【289】**多见于中年女性。临床表现以面颊部蝴蝶形皮疹、关节痛、肌肉痛、神经痛为特征。当有脑梗塞、脑出血时，可出现神经系统症状，如头痛、癫痫和精神异常等。**

【290】**【MRI征象】**

【291】**SLE 的 MRI 影像表现有四种类型：①限局性脑萎缩；②多发性脑梗塞；③位于皮层的斑块状长T、长T异常信号影：④位于皮层下的弥漫性斑片样长T、长Tz异常信号影。偶有钙化。斑片状异常信号影有“游走”性的特点，既数月后复查见原有的病灶消失，而在其它部位又出现新的病灶。**

【293】**第二十一节 播散性坏死性脑白质病**

【294】**播散性坏死性脑白质病 (disseminated necrotiging leukoencephalopathy) 是一脑白**

【296】**质广泛性脱髓鞘和坏死性疾病。**

【297】**【病因】**

【298】**本病是由于化学治疗(经蛛网膜下腔、脑室或静脉注射甲氨蝶呤)后引发的脑白质损害。**

【300】**本病病理特点为广泛性白质脱髓鞘、坏死和星形细胞增生等。病变区无炎性细胞浸润。**

【301】**\[临床表现】**

【305】**(高培毅 林 燕)**

【306】**第二十二节 亚急性硬化性全脑淡**

【307】**亚急性硬化性全脑炎 (subcute sclerosing panencephalitis， SSPE) 是由慢性病毒引起的一种特殊类型的感染后播散性全脑炎。**

【308】**【病因】**

【309】**一般认为是麻疹病毒感染后再活化所致。婴儿早期患麻疹，由于患儿此时仍有从母体带来的被动免疫力，故影响了主动免疫力的发展，不能产生特异性抗体，使病毒得以长期存于脑内，潜伏期可长达5~8年。以后由于机体细胞免疫力下降而发病。**

【310】**【病理】**

【311】**病理检查可见灰质内神经元减少、胶质细胞增生和血管周围淋巴细胞浸润；脑白质显示片状脱髓鞘和胶质增生。上述病理改变也可累及基底节、丘脑、桥脑和小脑。**

【312】**【临床表现】**

【313】**发病年龄多在5~21岁之间，尤以12岁以下儿童多见，大约85%的病人在3岁前患过麻疹。起病隐袭而渐进。主要表现为行为异常、进行性智力下降、肌阵挛和共济失调等，可有痴呆、癫痫。平均存活期为2~6年。个别病例病情发展迅速。**

【315】**主要表现为大脑半球皮层下白质区和基底节多发性斑片样异常信号强度影，病灶**

【316】**可波及小脑白质区。T加权像病灶显示为低信号或等信号影，Tz加权像为高信号强度。静脉注人对比剂后病变无增强。病程晚期可有广泛性脑萎缩。**

【344】**基底节及小脑齿状核的对称性钙化虽然在 CT上显示明显，但在MR影像上表现却多样。同一病例的不同部位，其钙化亦可表现不同的信号强度。T加权像钙化可为低或稍高信号强度影；Tz加权像则可表现为高或低信号强度(图12-13)。**

【345】**(高培毅 林 燕)**

【346】**第二十五节 一氧化碳中毒性脑病**

【347】**一氧化碳中毒性脑病 (carbon monoxide poisoning) 是指过量的一氧化碳进人血液后与血红蛋白结合形成碳氧血红蛋白，引起血液性缺氧导致脑组织损害。**

【348】**【病因】**

【349】**一氧化碳在空气中浓度超过 30mg/m'时就能发生中毒。冬季烧煤取暖、汽车尾气等均能接触一氧化碳。一氧化碳进人血液后与血红蛋白结合形成碳氧血红蛋白。由于一氧化碳与血红蛋白的亲和力比氧与血红蛋白的亲和力大300倍，且碳氧血红蛋白一经形成则不易分解，故造成低氧血症，导致脑组织缺氧并发生损害。**

【350】**【病理】**

【351】**缺氧导致脑血管壁细胞变性与血管运动神经麻痹、渗透性增高，引起脑水肿。随即出现点状出血、神经细胞变性、坏死及皮层下广泛脱髓鞘改变。**

【352】**【临床表现】**

【353】**轻度中毒者出现头痛、头胀、恶心、呕吐等症状；中度中毒者口唇呈樱桃红色、全身多汗，血压先升后降；重症者昏迷甚至死亡。**

【354】**【MRI 征象】**

【355】**一氧化碳中毒早期 MRI 检查见脑白质广泛性水肿，脑室系统变小；晚期常见双侧苍白球软化灶和脑菱缩表现。**

【356】**(高培教** **林** **燕)**

【357】**第二十六节 霉变甘蔗中华**

【358】**霉变甘蔗中毒(moldy sugar cane poisoning) 是由于食人发霉变质的甘蔗而引起**

【359】**的中枢神经系统中毒性病变。**

【360】**【病因】**

【361】**发霉变质的甘蔗中含有可产生3-硝基丙酸的节菱孢霉菌，当食人后，此种嗜神经毒素造成豆状核和脑皮质损害。**

【362】**【病理】**

【363】**主要病理表现为脑水肿、神经元和胶质细胞变性坏死，脑血管扩张，脑组织充血。**

【364】**\[临床表现】**

【365】**发病迅速，在食用发霉变质的甘蔗后30分钟内既可发生消化道症状，随即出现神经系统症状，如四肢抽搐、口吐白沫、神志不清和大小便失禁等。一周后可有低热。病情凶险，预后差。**

【366】**\[MRI征象】**

【367】**MRI 检查可见脑白质弥漫性水肿、双侧苍白球对称性肾形长T、长T异常信号影。**

【4】**Hirschsprung Disease (HD)**

【5】**Clinical Features**

【6】●UUncommon disease affecting 1 in 5000 to 30，000 live births

【7】上About 80% of patients are male

【8】**Small percentage of patients have other congenital anomalies**

【9】Presenting features include constipation， abdominal obstruction， meconium plug

【10】Patients with Down syndrome are at increased risk for HD

【11】Gross and Endoscopic Pathology

【12】●Classic resected colon consists of a dilated(neurologically normal) proximal segment that narrows (hypoganglionated area) into a contracted(aganglionic) distal segment

【13】May produce toxic megacolon

【14】Multiple forms exist

【15】\- Short-segment HD： as little as 3 cm of distal rectum affected (most common form)

【16】Long-segment HD： extends beyond sigmoid colon， can involve entire colon and a variable length of small intestine (about 10% of patients)

【17】Histopathology

【18】●Absence of ganglion cells from the submucosal and myenteric plexuses

【19】**Hypertrophy of the mural nerves**

【20】·Long-segment HD may have normal caliber nerves and false-negative acetylcholinesterase stain (see later

【21】Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry

【22】●Acetylcholinesterase reactions (on frozen tissue)：patients with HD demonstrate coarse， irregular nerve fibers extending from the muscularis mucosae up into the lamina propria (normal tissue contains only thin fibers， which are only in muscularis mucosae

【23】Neuron-specific enolase (NSE) positive in ganglion cells； other immunostains (e.g.， Cathepsin D， PGP9.5， bcl-2) can decorate ganglion cells

【24】S-100 protein： Schwann cells show perinuclear positivity

【25】Other Techniques for Diagnosis

【26】Gene mutations detected in 50% of patients include inactivation mutation of RET oncogene， mutations in endothelin receptor B； at least nine other gene mutations have been implicated

【27】Differential Diagnosis

【28】**Hypoganglionosis**

【29】●(Can cause HD-like syndrome with megacolon

【30】No accepted definition， but should be diagnosed in patients with a substantial reduction in ganglion cell numbers compared with normal (40 to 80 myenteric neurons per l cm of bowel)； can be zonal

【31】Some examples of hypoganglionosis could be similar to idiopathic constipation

【32】Intestinal neuronal dysplasia

【33】Clinically mimics HD， and patients typically present with constipation

【34】Differentiated by presence of hyperplastic plexuses and giant ganglia containing more than seven neurons

【35】Diagnostic criteria and even the existence of intestinal neuronal dysplasia debated

【36】●Diagnosis should be reserved for florid cases

【37】Idiopathic constipation

【38】●(Occurs more often in females and produces intestinal pseudo-obstruction

【39】Ganglion cells are present； distinctive abnormalities of the myenteric plexus (e.g.， loss of argyrophilic neurons) described

【40】Reduced volume of interstitial cells of Cajal reported in some cases

【41】**Pearls**

【42】●FBiopsy specimens in actual cases of HD usually contain hypertrophic nerves， but their presence is not diagnostic

【43】There can be overlap in the histologic changes described in intestinal neuronal dysplasia and neurofibromatosis

【53】**Diverticular Disease**

【54】**Clinical Features**

【55】●Most common in societies consuming a Western-style diet (high fat， low fiber)

【56】**In the United States， 50% of adults older than 40vears are affected**

【57】Only 20% of patients have symptoms； particularly obese individuals OD

【58】**Formation of diverticula is related to weakness in the colonic wall and increased intraluminal pressure**

【59】Symptoms may be related to diverticulitis， which includes lower abdominal pain， rebound tenderness， and fever； symptoms can occur without inflammation

【60】Patients may have symptoms related to anemia from chronic hemorrhage or have massive acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding

【61】Complications include obstruction， perforation， peritonitis， hemorrhage， abscess formation， and fistula

【62】**Mucosal prolapse is common in patients with diverticular disease**

【64】Small oval or spherical outpouchings along the large intestine

【65】About 90% involve the sigmoid colon

【66】Typically form adjacent to penetrating mural arteries and alongside taeniae coli

【67】**●Adjacent muscularis propria may be thickened**

【69】●Classic lesion is a protrusion of the mucosa and submucosa through the muscularis propria

【70】Diverticula may have a flattened or atrophic mucosa and compressed submucosa

【71】Adjacent tissue， including the muscular propria， is hypertrophied， fibrotic， and chronically intlamed

【72】**Acute inflammation indicates acute diverticulitis； may form peridiverticular abscesses**

【78】Inflammatory bowel disease (particularly Crohn disease)

【79】●Both conditions may cause focal mucosal inflammation and thickening of the bowel wall with stricture and fistula； conditions may coexist

【80】**Crohn disease is distinguished by fissural ulcers， ulcers and mucosal inflammation outside of the areas of diverticulitis， transmural inflammation， serosal lymphoid aggregates， superficial aphthous ulcers， and granulomas**

【90】**Eosinophilic Gastroenteritis**

【91】**Clinical Features**

【92】Syndrome characterized by gastrointestinal symptoms combined with eosinophilic infiltration of the gastrointestinal tract in the absence of a specific allergen or parasitic infestation， usually seen in children and young adults

【93】Most patients have peripheral blood eosinophilia(70% of cases)

【94】Most patients have a history of allergies

【95】Patients present with variable symptoms ranging from mild nausea and vomiting to an acute abdomen

【96】Other symptoms include diarrhea， malabsorption， obstruction， or ascites (often depends on level of the bowel wall involved)

【97】**●(Often have elevation of serum IL-5 levels**

【98】Gross and Endoscopic Pathology

【99】●Affects any level of gastrointestinal tract； stomach and small bowel are most common sites；less commonly affects the colon

【100】Radiographic studies often disclose widened mucosal folds and mural thickening

【101】Diffuse involvement may occur， producing bowel rigidity and edema

【102】Histopathology

【103】●Three patterns of eosinophilic gastroenteritis described

【104】\-Mucosal involvement typically causing diarrhea and malabsorption

【105】**_一_ Submucosal involvement associated with intestinal obstruction**

【106】Mural and serosal involvement leading to ascites and eosinophilic peritonitis

【107】●DDiffuse， sheetlike infiltrate of eosinophils typically involving the lamina propria， crypts， or villi

【108】Often associated with mucosal edema， crypt hyperplasia， or villous atrophy

【109】AMural fibrosis or muscular hypertrophy can occurSSerosal involvement may induce subserosal fibrosis

【110】Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry●1Noncontributory

【111】Other Techniques for Diagnosis

【112】**●Noncontributory**

【113】Differential Diagnosis

【114】●1Numerous diseases present with eosinophilic infiltrates； rule out allergies， lymphoma， foreign bodies， systemic vasculitis， drug reaction， and parasitic infestation

【115】Cow's milk allergy

【116】Typically affects neonatal or young infants with sensitivity to milk protein； generally responds to prompt switch to soy-based or hydrolysate formula

【117】●Infants present with severe diarrhea， dehydration， and failure to thrive

【118】Characterized by villous atrophy， neutrophilic infiltrates， and eosinophilic infiltrate

【119】Overall prognosis is excellent

【120】Other food allergies

【121】Affects 45% of the population and nearly 10% of children

【122】Histologically similar to eosinophilic gastroenteritis

【123】Requires correlation of symptoms with exposure to a specific food

【124】**Pearls**

【125】●Resist temptation to suggest eosinophilic gastroenteritis at the sight of eosinophils， which are a normal component of the gastrointestinal muicosa

【126】\- Collections of eosinophils not associated with other inflammatory cells， groupings of eosinophils associated with mucosal architectural change or injury (e.g.， crypt abscesses)， and infiltration of the muscularis mucosae and deeper bowel layers are all considered abnormal and in a corroborative clinical setting should be considered diagnostic of eosinophilic gastroenteritis

【127】Whenever collections of eosinophils are seen， it makes sense to check for parasites

【136】Characterized by immunologic reaction between(engrafted) donor T lymphocytes and epithelial cells of recipient (host)

【206】Gross and Endoscopic Pathology

【207】**Crohn disease**

【208】●Involves any level of gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus； classically affects the small bowel

【209】Mesenteric fat of the involved segment wraps around the bowel surface (“creeping fat” or “fat wrapping")

【210】Thickened， stiff intestinal wall (stovepipe) with normal-appearing intervening segments (skip lesions)

【211】Early disease is characterized by aphthous ulcers that progress to discrete ulceration， serpiginous ulcers， linear ulcers， or cobblestoning

【212】Cobblestoning results from two different ulceration patterns： linear ulcers and small horizontal crevices. The sharp demarcation between edematous but otherwise normal mucosa and surrounding ulcers gives the mucosa a cobblestone appearance

【213】Ulcers deepen into fissures and can ultimately produce fistulas

【214】Luminal narrowing often causes characteristic string sign on x-ray

【215】**Ulcerative colitis**

【216】●【Classically demonstrates involvement of the rectum and variable length of large intestine (without skip lesions)

【217】Often involves the entire colon (pan-colitis) and occasionally spills into ileum (so-called backwash ileitis)； in some classification schemes， ileal involvement is a criterion for inflammatory bowel disease of indeterminate type

【218】Irregular areas of ulceration， which may be widespread， can surround islands of preserved mucosa (pseudopolyps and inflammatory polyps)

【219】**Deep ulcers extending to the muscularis externa usually correlate with fulminant clinical disease and are a pathologic criterion for inflammatory bowel disease of an indeterminate type in some schemes**

【220】Normal serosa unless complicated by fulminant disease

【221】**Crohn disease**

【222】Classic features include patchy， transmural chronic inflammation with intervening normal areas (skip lesions)

【223】●上Acute inflammatory fissures penetrate the muscularis externa

【225】Granulomas occur in up to 50% cases， both in actively involved and uninvolved tissue

【226】In chronic disease， Paneth cell and pyloric metaplasia OCCUr

【227】Neutrophilic infiltrates and crypt abscesses may OCCUr

【230】●CCharacterized by a dense lymphoplasmacytic and neutrophilic infiltrate

【86】**Preface**

【87】**The aims of this book are threefold. First， to provide the undergraduate sludent with vicarious experiences that will temporarily fill the void that will later be filled by the student’s own experiences. Second， Lo offer ther-apists， whether students or vastly experienced， the chance to challenge themselves against case histories in private to see how they do. I know that self-testing is something that few physical therapists can pass up. Third， unusual cases are exactly that， unusual. We do not individually have many opportunities to see many patienls with cancers， gastric ul-cers， kidney stones， hiatus hernias， and the like， so we tend to miss them becausc our orthopedic blinkers focus everything into orthopedic condi-tions. If this book does nothing more than help you realize that oddities have a way of presenting as the mundane and that we have a way of per-ceiving what we expect rather than what is， it will have been successful.**

【88】**This is not a how-to book in the conventional sense of instruction in the techniques or examination. In general educational terms， this re-quirement is dealt with in school and in a plethora of books designed for exactly this purpose. However， what the student cannot gain in the classroom is experience. During clinical placemenis， the student is quite correctly required to rotale through the various specialties and so re-ceives comparatively little experience in orthopedics and often none at all in orthopedic manual therapy. The schools know that when the newly graduated therapist is ready to specialize in one area， postgraduate pro-grams are available. Unfortunately， other than clinical residencies， these classes still lack what is missing in the physical therapy school， hands-on experience. The object of this book is to try to teach how to analyzc and integrate information gained from subjective and objective clinical examinations. It will help the student and practitioner of orthopedic physical therapy to differentiale patients with routine diagnoses， treat-ment plans， and responses to trealment from those who will be a prob-lem to the therapist. These latter patients must be identified early so that a nonroutine approach can be taken. If physical therapy is appropriate， a unique approach can be designed for the more difficult patient. If or-thopedic therapy is deemed inappropriate， the patient can be returned to the physician as quickly as possible.**

【89】**To succeed in these aims， the first section of the book will consist of one clinical approach to the evaluation of the neuromusculoskeletal sys-tem. The first chapter gencrally describes the differential diagnostic**

【90】**examination and discusses the integration of the data generated from the examination. From this integration， the therapist can either generate a working diagnosis and a management plan or determine that further clin-ical examination is required. For example， from the differential diag-nostic examination a working diagnosis might be an L4 disk extrusion with L5 spinal nerve compression with radiculopathy. From this diag-nosis， a treatment plan can be made that might consist of specific exer-cises， traction， rest， and so on， or inappropriate pathology might be sus-pected and the patient returned to the physician. Alternatively， and usually more commonly， a set of signs and symptoms that do not lend themselves to a specific diagnosis are found. In this case further infor-mation is required before a specific treatment plan can be arrived at. This information is afforded by the biomechanical examination. Exam-ples of the type of diagnosis that can be arrived at from the biome-chanical examination include a right L4-5 zygapophyseal joint hypo-mobility， a right L3-4 torsional instability， or a left C5-6 zygapophyseal joint extension hypermobility. From this biomechanical evaluation， the therapist can initiate a specific exercise program， manual therapy， and/or stabilization treatments.**

【91】**The differential diagnostic examination， designed by James Cyriax， M.D.， will be， with very slight modifications， possibly the most com-prehensive and rational clinical examination of the musculoskeletal sys-tem in use today. The modifications are simply additions that will in-crease the breadth of the diagnostic scope. The examination is based on our knowledge of the anatomy of the musculoskeletal system. The func-tion of each subset of the system， such as the contractile tissues (mus-cle， tendon， and tenoperiosteal junction)， the inert tissues (joint capsule， ligament， dura， bone， and bursa)， the vascular system (arteries and veins)， and the neurological system (peripheral and central systems) is stressed. The test stress is the function of the subset applied in as much as iso-lation from the other subsets as is possible.**

For example， paresthesia will be discussed in general terms in Chapler 1 and mention will be made of its significance， but how the pattern of paresthesia suggests certain conditions will be discussed in detail in the discussion of a particular case.**
