【97】**The Orthopedic Physical Therapist's Differential Diagnosis Examination**

【98】**Increasingly， physical therapists are being called upon to act as screen-ing professionals for orthopedic patients. More and more therapists are legally entitled to provide primary care when the apparent safety net of the physician referral is absent. As commonly as， or perhaps more com-monly than primary contact， the family physician is relying on the ther-apist to “assess and treat" rather than follow a predetermined diagnosis and a set formula of therapy.**

【99】**The subject of physical therapists making differential diagnoses is con-troversial. There is some genuine concern for the patient here， but there is also considerable turf protecting going on. From a patient concern per-spective there is little to take issue with when the therapist makes the dif-ferential diagnoses. If the physician makes a referral and the therapist disagrees with the proffered diagnosis and sends the patient back， what harm has been done? Is the therapist capable of making a differential di-agnosis， or at least recognizing red flags and sending them to the physi-cian? In Britain a study was undertaken comparing outcomes and patient satisfaction between orthopedic physical therapists licensed to give steroid injections and orthopedic surgeons in a hospital outpatient de-partment. The abstract gave the result as this： “An appropriately trained physiotherapist is as effective as staff grade surgeons in managing or-thopedic out-patients unlikely to benefit from surgical intervention?\***

【100】**There is no doubt that it is the physician’s responsibility to provide as precise a medical diagnosis as possible and to communicate that di-agnosis to the patient and the therapist. However， the physician’s re-sponsibility to make the diagnosis does not abrogate the therapist’s re-sponsibility to ensure that that diagnosis is correct and that the referral is appropriate. With the possible exception of postsurgical referrals from neuro- and orthopedic surgeons， it is unusual to receive a precise and accurate diagnosis from a referring physician. More commonly， the**

【101】**\*Weale AE， Bannister GC： Who should see orthopedic outpatients-physiotherapisis or** **surgeons? Ann R Coll Surg Engl 72(Suppl 2)：71， 1995.**

【102】**prescription simply states “assess and treat." When a nonsurgical diag-nosis is afforded， it is often of little value to the therapist as far as the determination of a treatment regimen is concerned. Such clinically val- _ueless diagnoses include low back pain， acute low back pain， shoulder_ _impingement syndrome， rotator cuff syndrome， deranged knee， torticol-lis， back strain， chest wall pain， ankle sprain， and so forth. These types_ of “diagnoses” do nothing more than regurgitate the patient’s symptoms or the mechanism of injury or the area of pain. Even apparently precise diagnoses such as tennis elbow or the more technical lateral epicondylitis often do not help in determining treatment， as they are not precise enough. Take for an example luteral epicondylitis. Unless the exact lo-cation is known， effective treatment cannot be carried out. Is it supra-condylar， epicondylar， in the tendon body， or at the myotendonous junc-tion? Is it primary or secondary? If it is secondary， does the neck need treatment or is there a biomechanical problem at the elbow causing or contributing to the symptomatic lesion? Only a detailed examination of the patient， an in-depth analysis of the information generated from the examination， and the subsequent generation of a differential diagnosis will provide this information， which is so vital to efficient and effective treaiment.**

【103】**The problem is compounded by direct access. In some countries， no-tably Australia and the United Kingdom， and in some states and provinces in the United States and Canada， the therapist has the right of direct access to the patient without referral from the physician. In one or two of these jurisdictions in the United States， this same therapist who can see the patient without referral does not have the right to make a differential diagnosis. This is obviously a silly state of affairs. How can anybody of any discipline see patients as a primary care practitioner without making a diagnosis? To get around this stupidity， the therapists _use the terms physical therapy diagnosis or functional diagnosis. So_ somehow， a disk prolapse ceases to exist when it is examined by a ther-apist but is present when assessed by a physician. It is of course im-possible for the orthopedic therapist to treat any patient effectively， ef-ficiently， or even ethically without previously examining the patient and coming to some conclusion concerning the patient’s condition. It is time to realize that making a diagnosis is common to all health care profes-sionals involved in the treatment of patients， not just physicians， and is not in and of itself practicing medicine. Regardless of what euphemisms are currently being employed to conform with state， provincial， or even national regulations regarding the right and ability of the physical ther-apist to make a differential diagnosis， that is exactly what we have to do in order to treat the patient appropriately.**

【104】**To do this， the therapist must be able to sort through the masses of data generated during both the objective and subjective examinations to reach a provisional working diagnosis that will facilitate the formation**

【105】**of a rational management plan. This plan should be based on the clini-cal presentation of the patient and the state of the art information about the function of the body， the pathological processes that the patient is undergoing， and the therapist's experience and skill level.**

【44】**Cordella， Dickerson， Quimby， Yunusova， and Green (2017) compared the three variants of PPA with quantitative measures of speech rate. Articulation rate was the most effective for differentiating between nfPPA and the more fluent lPPA and SD groups. The diagnostic accuracy of quantified speech and articulation rate measures was noticeably better than that of the clinician rating scale of the speech impairment. Further articulation rate was the best classifier overall. Slowing of speech， therefore， is one of the best predictors of nfPPA； however， the discrimination between 1PPA and SD cannot be based on speech rate alone. It should also be noted that reduced speech rate could be due to akinesia and bradyphrenia. Therefore slowing of speech is also a common symptom of atypical Parkinson’s disease like PSP， CBD/CBS， and nfPPA. An additional feature of patients with nfPPA is that they seemingly have problems expressing their thoughts during communication. Such a behavior is not char-acteristic for atypical Parkinson’s patients. Marshall et al. (2018) developed a short decision tree to distinguish between the PPAs， relying on specific symp-toms of nfPPA patients. This decision tree is called effortful speech and the existence of dysarthria or speech apraxia (Fig. 5.4).**

【46】**5.3.3 Language comprehension**

【47】**The language impairment of nfPPA patients is not confined to the production of words and sentences (Table 5.1). They also have problems understanding complex sentences but not of single words， at least during the beginning of their disease. Peelle et al. (2008) showed that nfPPA patients have problems understanding grammatically complex sentences and constructing sentences from written words， which are related to the content of a picture (Weintraub et al.， 2009).**

【48】**Charles et al. (2014) compared the specific understanding problems of nfPPA patients with those of lPPA， SD， and bvFTD patients. 1PPA and SD patients have problems with sentence understanding. As such， the main question was what aspects of language might be responsible for these com-prehension differences. Therefore Charles et al. (2014) varied two features which could have an impact on comprehension. The first feature concerns working memory. If working memory is the cause of an understanding def-icit then a more or less linear relation between the length of the sentence and the impairment should be present. Working memory is influenced by duration and complexity. Hence Charles et al. (2014) used sentences such as “The octopus was jolly and it trailed the seahorse" and “The fox that followed the domesticated cat was fierce." Both sentences are similar in length， however， in the second sentence， the main message is interrupted by additional (center) information. Charles and colleagues predicted that if working memory is the source of the understanding deficit then the patients should be more impaired in the second sentence. However， understanding can also be impaired by problems in understanding semantic relations of agents and contexts. Evaluate， for example， the sentence“It was the excited boy that the girl watched.” This sentence was also presented by Charles et al. and has the same length as the two aforementioned sen-tences. In this sentence， however， the agents are changing (there is a cleft shifting from “excited boy” to “watching girl"). Therefore this sentence can only be understood if the recipients can follow the contextual structure of its meaning.**

【49】**The result of this study was clear-cut. All PPA patient groups had more problems in understanding sentences than the healthy controls. All patient groups also had problems with parentheses in the center of a sen-tence but had no specific problems with the length of the sentences. On the other hand， only the performance of the nfPPA group decreased sig-nificantly relative to the existence of agents or context shift by clefts in the sentences. Thus the verbal understanding of allpatients'groups dropped relative to the existence of an interruption of the sentence but only the nfPPA group suffered from additional problems when the gram-matical structure forced them to reorganize the sentence according to meaning changes.**

【50】**5.3.4Other cognitive features of nonfluent primary progressive aphasia**

【51】**In the study from Gunawardena et al. (2010)， bvFTD and nfPPA patients were both impaired in categorial word fluency and in phonological word flu-ency， however， nfPPA patients were significantly more impaired during word fluency tasks than bvFTD patients. nfPPA patients also suffered from higher deficits in the Stroop interference task (a test that involves naming)， in the trail making test B (TMT B； a test that involves verbal working mem-ory)， and in the Boston naming task. On the other hand， bvFTD patients showed significantly higher deficits in accessing semantic relations of pre-sented pictures compared to nfPPA patients. This pattern of results highlights the dominant problem of nfPPA patients， accessing， and maintaining the pho-nological word form， in contrast to their better semantic understanding.**

【52】Marra et al. (2007) compared bvFTD， nfPPA， and AD patients using numeroouuss neuropsychological tests. As expected， AD patients generally exhibited significantly higher impairments in delayed recall and recognition tasks. nfPPA patientss were impaired in phonological word fluency and Stroop interference compared to the two other groups. These results concur with those from Gunawardena et al. (2010). According to Blair， Marczinski， Davis-Faroque， and Kertesz (2007)， who compared patients with nfPPA， bvFTD and AD over a period of 2 years， the language abilities of patients with nfPPA decline faster than in bvFTD and AD patients.

【53】**Butts et al. (2015) compared the three variants of PPA by means of sev-eral neuropsychological tests. In memory tests， nfPPA patients outperformed the lPPA patients， showing no difference to the SD patients. One exception， however， was the Rey-Osterrieth figure copying test in which SD patients achieved significantly better scores than nfPPA patients. Moreover the nfPPA patients were almost significantly slower in the TMT A tests com-pared to the SD patients. For the language tasks， nfPPA produced fewer words in phonological word fluency compared to the SD patients.**

【54】**Showing more pronounced declines of language functions and abilities for communicating， nfPPA patients are relatively free of behavioral distur-bances. Marra et al. (2007) not only relied on neuropsychological tests but also included the neuropsychiatric inventory to compare nfPPA， bvFTD， and AD patients. nfPPA were almost free of any behavioral disorder， except for showing increased apathy. On the other hand， bvFTD patients documented more agitated behavior， apathy， disinhibition， and eating disorders.**

【0】性啰音，与哨笛音相似，其特点为吸气时间正常或稍短，而呼气时间明显延长，同时布满双侧肺野。其次要分清干性啰音在双侧肺野是满布的还是局部的。如双侧肺野布满干性啰音，见于广泛性支气管狭窄如支气管哮喘或慢性阻塞性肺疾病等。局部经常存在的干性啰音则是局限病变伴有支气管狭窄的特征，见于支气管内膜结核、支气管扩张症以及肺癌等疾病。

【1】### 二、产生干性啰音的常见疾病

【2】临床上，很多疾病可产生干性啰音，如急性支气管炎、慢性支气管炎、慢性阻塞性肺疾病、支气管异物、肺炎、支气管哮喘、心源性哮喘、肺结核以及肺癌等，应根据其临床特点进行仔细的鉴别。

【3】##### 1.慢性支气管炎

【4】慢性支气管炎（chronic bronchitis）是指气管、支气管黏膜及其周围组织的慢性非特异性炎症。以咳嗽、咳痰或伴有喘息及反复发作的慢性过程为特征。病程较长，病情进展缓慢，以老年人为多发。在患者的急性发作期可有散在的干性啰音，其特点常为双侧肺野均可闻及，常伴有湿性啰音，且以湿性啰音为主，伴有呼气相延长。干性和湿性啰音多出现在背部及双肺底部，部位不恒定，在咳嗽后可减少或消失。

【5】##### 2.慢性阻塞性肺疾病

【6】慢性阻塞性肺疾病（chronic obstructive pulmonary disease）是一种气流受限性疾病。在临床表现上与慢性支气管炎极为相似，但慢性支气管炎并不存在气流受限。因此，在临床上，慢性阻塞性肺疾病患者出现的干性啰音的特点与慢性支气管炎相同，但慢性阻塞性肺疾病患者常可见桶状胸和双肺呼吸音降低。

【7】##### 3.支气管哮喘

【8】支气管哮喘（bronchial asthma）是一种以嗜酸性粒细胞、肥大细胞反应为主的气道慢性炎症性疾病，以气道高反应性为特征。其主要症状为发作性伴有哮鸣音的呼气性呼吸困难或发作性胸闷和咳嗽，严重者被迫采取坐位或呈端坐呼吸，干咳，甚至出现发绀等。其干性啰音的特点为阵发性出现，表现为双侧肺野有广泛的哮鸣音，并伴呼气音延长，常可见双肺呈过度充气的表现，在疾病缓解时这类改变可完全恢复正常。但应注意，在轻度哮喘发作或非常严重的哮喘发作，哮鸣音可不出现。

【9】##### 4.心源性哮喘

【10】心源性哮喘（cardiac asthma）常见于左心功能衰竭，患者多有高血压、冠状动脉粥样硬化性心脏病、风湿性心脏病和二尖瓣狭窄等病史和体征。患者常为急性起病，呈阵发性咳嗽，常咳出粉红色泡沫痰，伴出汗多或表现为大汗淋漓，需采取端坐位，两肺可闻广泛的湿性啰音和哮鸣音，左心界扩大，心率增快，心尖部可闻及奔马律。病情允许可做胸部X线检查时，可见心脏增大以及肺淤血征。

【11】##### 5.支气管肺癌

【12】支气管肺癌（bronchogenic carcinoma）中心型肺癌伴感染或类癌综合征时，可出现喘鸣或哮喘样呼吸困难。或因肿瘤压迫气管或支气管，造成狭窄或不完全阻塞，均可引起干性啰音。肺癌所致的呼吸困难及喘鸣症状常呈进行性加重，一般无明显诱因，咳嗽可伴有血痰，痰中可找到癌细胞。胸部X线摄片、CT或MRI检查或纤支镜检查常可明确诊断。

【13】##### 6.变态反应性肺浸润

【14】变态反应性肺浸润（allergic pulmonary infiltration）患者多有致病原接触史，致病原常为寄生虫、花粉或职业粉尘等。患者的症状相对较轻，部分患者可听到干性啰音。患者常有发热，胸部X线检查可见多发性、此起彼伏的淡薄斑片浸润阴影，可自发消失或再发。肺组织活检也有助于鉴别。

【15】##### 7.支气管扩张症

【16】支气管扩张症（bronchiectasis）具有慢性咳嗽、咳痰以及咯血反复发作的特点，合并感染时有大量脓痰。患者病程一般较长，多以青少年时期起病，逐渐加重，肺部可出现干性啰音，但更多表现为肺部湿性啰音，其特点是出现啰音的部位相对固定，多见于下肺，与慢性支气管炎出现的弥漫性和非恒定性啰音形成对比，病程较长者可有杵状指（趾）。胸部X线检查常见一侧或双侧下肺纹理粗乱呈卷发状，支气管造影或高分辨CT检查可以明确诊断。

【17】##### 8.肺结核

【18】肺结核（pulmonary tuberculosis）患者临床表现不尽相同。常有结核中毒症状或局部症状如发热、乏力、盗汗、消瘦、咳嗽以及咯血等表现。经X线检查和痰结核菌检查可以明确诊断。部分患者肺部出现干性啰音，尤其是存在支气管内膜结核时，由于气道部分狭窄，可出现干性啰音，其特点为啰音部位相对固定，且较少出现湿性啰音。

【32】# 第十章 杵状指/

【33】第十章　杵状指
=======

【34】早在公元前400年，“医学之父”希波克拉底即认识到了肺气肿患者伴发的杵状指现象。杵状指（finger clubbing或digital clubbing）是指（趾）末端鼓槌状膨大，指（趾）甲的纵脊及横脊弯曲隆起呈表玻璃样，又被称为希波克拉底指（趾）（Hippocratic fingers），表玻璃样指（趾）（watch-glass nails），或者鼓槌样指（趾）（drumstick fingers）。

【35】# 第十章 杵状指/第一节 病 因

【36】第一节　病　因
-------

【37】杵状指可以单独发生，也可以作为肥大性（增生性）骨关节病（hypertrophic osteoarthropathy，HOA）的体征之一合并出现。HOA是一组以长骨骨膜增生（骨赘形成），关节疼痛和杵状指形成为特征的综合征。原发性HOA又称为厚皮性骨膜病（pachydermoperiostosis），是一种常染色体显性遗传的病变，患者全身情况良好，除了杵状指、骨赘形成和皮肤改变外无其他异常发现。皮肤的病变包括皮肤的粗糙增厚，多汗以及脂溢性皮炎等。但患者表现为不完全型时，可以单纯表现为杵状指或者骨膜增生或厚皮病。文献报道的家族性杵状指很有可能就是不完全型的原发性HOA。

【38】继发性HOA的临床表现和原发性HOA类似，从单纯的杵状指到合并骨膜增生、关节病变不等，可并发于多种疾患，多为双侧对称改变。但也有单侧杵状指、单个杵状指的报道。单侧杵状指常见于神经和血管病变的并发症。

【41】# 第十章 杵状指/第二节 发生机制

【42】第二节　发生机制
--------

【43】杵状指最初表现为甲周红斑和甲床软化，触之有海绵感；继而甲床和指骨间的角度从正常的160°进行性加大，指端末梢膨大并使甲背呈弓背形弯曲；最后指（趾）甲光泽度增强并有纵脊形成，使整个甲床呈表玻璃样改变。整个变化过程可以历时数年而呈慢性病程，也可以迅速出现表现为亚急性发作。

【44】在显微镜下观察，杵状指表现为弥散性血管内皮增生，部分毛细血管的管腔闭塞，毛细血管周围见淋巴组织细胞浸润，胶原纤维沉积，血管壁增厚变硬，并伴有皮脂腺和汗腺肥大。毛细血管镜发现杵状指有更多更大的毛细血管丛形成，并伴有更多的分支。对杵状指进行血管造影也发现手指杵状改变后微血管明显增多，具体表现为小动脉和动静脉吻合增生。杵状指的磁共振血管成像（MR angiography）也提示了类似的表现。

【45】杵状指（趾）形成的机制尚未明了。循环末梢指端缺氧，通过血管活性物质如缓激肽、前列腺素、铁蛋白、羟色胺或三磷腺苷等的作用，使局部血管扩张，组织增殖，是目前较为公认的杵状指（趾）形成机制。慢性肺部疾病及先天性心脏疾病的组织缺氧；炎症及肿瘤致血流中纤维蛋白原和球蛋白增加，使红细胞接触面减少而引起组织缺氧等，使局部血管扩张及血流增快，代谢旺盛，耗氧增加，组织增生等，形成杵状指（趾）。局部血流淤滞使有害物质易于滞留于指端并导致杵状指的形成。

【46】此外，还有一些其他的杵状指形成的假说，分述如下：

【47】##### 1.血小板相关学说

【48】血小板相关学说认为，骨髓巨核细胞在肺循环裂解成碎片并形成血小板，而一些心肺疾患可以干扰肺循环，从而使这些巨核细胞没有裂解而直接进入体循环，并因其较大的体积而淤积在指端末梢循环，此时巨核细胞及其碎片释放出血小板衍生生长因子（PDGF），PDGF可以增加血管壁通透性，使单核细胞和中性粒细胞活化以及大量血管平滑肌细胞和成纤维细胞增生，并最终导致杵状指的形成。而炎性肠病常常伴有血小板增生症（thrombocythemia），肝脏疾患伴有肺循环病变，通过这一学说也可以解释为什么在这些疾病中会出现杵状指。发绀型先天性心脏病和其他一些继发性HOA患者与对照组相比具有血小板计数减少和平均血小板体积增大，说明有较大的血小板和肺内巨核细胞裂解成碎片减少。尸解发现杵状指患者较对照者的指端循环有更多的微血栓形成，说明有更多的血小板活化。同时发现，原发性和继发性HOA患者较正常人和其他不伴有HOA的慢性肺部疾病患者，其PDGF水平明显增高。除了PDGF外，在继发性HOA患者体内还发现另外一种血小板衍生的可促进生长的血管内皮生长因子（VEGF），可能也与杵状指的形成相关。

【49】##### 2.慢性缺氧学说

【50】慢性缺氧致使指端血管扩张和血流增速，从而促进指端微循环血管内皮和平滑肌细胞增生，结缔组织过度生长，并进而引发末端指节的膨大和杵状改变。其可能机制是：①血流增速使流经指端的血液未能将所携带的氧释放出来，致局部组织缺氧；②指端局部温度增高，组织耗氧增加；③局部组织代谢旺盛，导致组织缺氧更为严重。

【51】##### 3.神经学说

【52】肺及胸膜疾病的传入神经冲动经肋间神经或迷走神经到达脑干，通过神经反射使指端组织血管扩张。

【53】##### 4.生长激素相关

【54】研究发现，伴发杵状指的支气管肺癌患者与未伴发杵状指的支气管肺癌患者相比较，其体内生长激素水平更高，因此，推测杵状指的发生可能与生长激素有关，但其他类似的试验又未能得出同样的结果。

【55】# 第十章 杵状指/第三节 诊断措施

【56】第三节　诊断措施
--------

【57】杵状指作为一种临床表现，伴发于其他疾病。在诊断过程中，应首先确定是否为杵状指，然后再分析其形成原因。

【58】### 一、确定诊断杵状指的定量指标

【59】临床上，对明显的杵状指（趾）诊断较为容易，但对轻度或者早期病变的诊断则存在一定的主观性。因此，为了提高诊断的准确性，有学者提出了一些客观的定量指标，其中，较为常用者包括以下几个。

【60】##### 1.轮廓角（profile angle）

【61】这是最早被提出来用于判断有无杵状指的客观指标。早在1938年，Livebond指出，正常人拇指的甲床和第一指节末端形成的基底角应当小于160°，如果大于180°，则考虑为手指杵状改变，这一角度被称为“轮廓角”或者“Livebond角”（Livebond angle），随后也同样用于拇指以外的其他手指（趾）。

【62】##### 2.修正轮廓角（modified profile angle）

【63】在中间指节和远端指节的背面切线相交所成的角度，正常应当约为160°，杵状指患者会减少到约145°。

【64】##### 3.甲下角（hyponychial angle）

【65】这一指标因为特异性高而被广泛采用，测量方法是做远端指间关节和甲床根部的连线，并与甲床根部和指间甲床下部分的连线相交所形成的角度。此角大于192°即可诊断为杵状指。

【66】##### 4.手指厚度比值（phalangeal depth ratio）

【67】用被检者手指远端指节的厚度与第一指间关节的厚度进行比较，如果比值大于1.0，则可诊断为杵状指。

【68】##### 5.NB/DIP比值

【69】采用手指甲床周径（nailbed circumference，NB）和第一指间关节的周径（distal interphalangeal joint circumference，DIP）相比，如果比值大于1.0，可诊断为杵状指。也可将双手十个手指的NB/DIP值相加，如果总和大于10，也可诊断杵状指。

【70】##### 6.Schamroth征（Schamroth sign）

【71】将被检者双手拇指背部互相贴紧，可以观察到在甲床和指间关节间形成一菱形的空隙，而在杵状指患者这一空隙明显变小甚至消失。

【72】发现杵状指（趾）后，需根据是单侧杵状指还是双侧杵状指进行病因的分析和鉴别诊断。详细的病史采集和体格检查对诊断和鉴别诊断具有重要意义。杵状指以外的其他症状和体征将决定鉴别诊断的方向以及应采取的进一步辅助检查项目。

【73】### 二、病　史

【74】仔细的病史采集，有助于为诊断杵状指的病因提供线索。在问诊过程中，应注意以下一些方面的问题。

【75】##### 1.杵状指的发病时间

【76】自幼发生的杵状指常见于发绀型先天性心脏病和原发性HOA，迟显性发绀患者如艾森曼格综合征患者杵状指和发绀一样出现较迟。其他继发性HOA或获得性杵状指往往伴发于呼吸系统疾患或慢性疾病，且出现较晚。如果患者偏瘫病史之后出现单侧杵状指，要考虑偏瘫引发杵状指的可能，对单侧杵状指患者还要注意询问外伤史，血液透析造瘘史等。

【77】##### 2.杵状指的伴随症状

【78】根据原发疾病的不同，杵状指的发病有各自不同的伴随症状。肺源性疾患伴发杵状指的患者多数有气短、乏力、咳嗽、咳痰、咯血以及胸痛等呼吸系统症状和低氧血症；肺部恶性肿瘤伴发杵状指的患者还可以有副癌综合征的其他表现，如异位激素综合征、类癌综合征等；心源性疾病伴发杵状指的患者往往伴发心悸、发绀、劳力性呼吸困难以及心力衰竭等表现；炎性肠病伴发杵状指的患者多有腹痛、腹泻、腹部包块、大便异常等；肝硬化或肝脏肿瘤伴发杵状指的患者除有肝功能异常如黄疸、厌油、乏力、腹痛等表现外，还可以有肝肺综合征的相关表现，当患者在肝病基础上出现呼吸困难，不明原因的低氧血症时，应当注意排除本病。对双侧杵状指患者，首先应当明确患者有无杵状指的家族史，并排除原发性HOA的可能性。患者是否合并骨痛和关节炎对诊断也十分重要。研究发现，继发性HOA中，如表现为全部手指杵状指，并伴有骨膜增生和关节痛的患者，约90%已有或即将有恶性肿瘤病变，故对此类患者应特别重视。

【79】##### 3.问诊要点

【80】在病史采集过程中，除询问以上两个方面外，应对以下一些情况进行重点询问：①杵状指的发病年龄、起病时间，出现急缓，病情进展情况；②杵状指分布与范围，是全身性抑或局部性；是双侧对称性还是单侧甚至单个手指（趾）；③是否有杵状指的家族史；④有无关节炎和骨痛表现，如有则注意排除胸腔内恶性病变尤其是肺癌的可能性，询问有无咳嗽、咯血、胸痛情况；⑤逐步排除心肺疾患、消化系统疾患的可能性，完善的系统回顾是十分重要的。

【81】### 三、体格检查

【82】单侧杵状指排除偏瘫时应注意患者有无神经系统体征如面瘫、单侧肢体感觉或运动障碍，对怀疑单侧血管病变时，应当注意对比双侧脉搏的对称性，寻找有无血管杂音。

【83】双侧杵状指患者应首先排除继发性HOA，其具体表现与原发疾病相关。

【84】##### 1.肺源性肥大性骨关节病

【85】胸廓形状改变、上腔静脉综合征、气管位置改变、胸部叩诊音异常、呼吸音异常、出现Velcro爆裂音以及恶病质等。

【86】##### 2.心脏疾患

【87】合并中心性发绀，心界长大，震颤，心律异常，心音改变，如第二心音增强或者减弱，明显的心脏杂音，血管杂音，颈静脉怒张，水肿以及心源性腹水。

【88】##### 3.胃肠道疾患

【89】局限性腹部压痛、腹块、肠鸣音改变以及腹部膨隆等。

【90】##### 4.肝脏疾病

【91】肝硬化的典型体征包括肝病面容，肝掌、蜘蛛痣，黄疸，肝源性腹水，腹壁静脉曲张，脾脏长大，男性乳房发育，瘀点、瘀斑甚至血肿形成等。

【92】##### 5.甲状腺病变

【93】突眼，甲状腺肿大，甲状腺眼征，心率快，胫前水肿等。

【94】##### 6.血液系统疾患

【95】外周浅表淋巴结肿大，出血倾向，胸骨叩痛，贫血等。

【96】### 四、辅助检查

【97】##### 1.骨和关节X线检查

【98】合并骨痛、关节肿痛的患者应对局部进行X线筛查，确认病变性质，明确有无骨膜增生和关节炎性改变。

【99】##### 2.胸部影像学检查

【100】是筛查病因最为重要的检查之一，可以初步判断病变部位是肺部、心脏或者纵隔改变，部分疾病可以明确病因。对于高度怀疑是肺部或纵隔病变的患者，胸部CT甚至高分辨CT扫描是更具诊断意义的检查方法。

【101】##### 3.肺功能检查

【102】了解肺的通气/换气、弥散功能状况，从而帮助明确引起杵状指的病因。

【103】##### 4.超声心动图检查

【104】对怀疑心脏疾患的患者应当常规进行此项检查，以明确先天性心脏病或感染性心内膜炎的诊断，并可指导治疗。

【105】##### 5.心电图检查

【106】对了解心脏房室改变和心律情况具有有一定的辅助诊断价值。

【107】##### 6.心导管检查

【108】对于各种先天性心脏病，尤其是超声心动图检查不能明确诊断者，或者需要判断心腔和大血管压力，明确分流量以帮助决定手术方式者，可以进行此项检查。但因其为有创性和费用昂贵而不作为常规筛查方式。

【109】##### 7.消化道内镜检查

【110】怀疑炎性肠病的患者需行肠镜检查，而肝硬化合并消化道出血患者，上消化道内镜也是重要的检查项目。

【111】##### 8.腹部超声检查和腹部CT扫描

【112】对怀疑消化系统疾病引起者，具有一定的诊断价值。

【113】##### 9.血液学检查

【114】血常规检查可以对血液系统疾患进行初步的筛查，同时了解有无贫血、血小板减少或者红细胞增多症等。而血液生化检查则有助于了解肝、肾功能状态。对杵状指患者应该常规进行这两项检查。

【115】# 第十章 杵状指/第四节 鉴别诊断

【116】第四节　鉴别诊断
--------

【117】由于引起杵状指的病因众多，对于一个存在杵状指的患者，应仔细进行分析，寻找出引起的原因。有关单侧和双侧杵状指的鉴别诊断流程见图10-1和图10-2。

【118】图10-1　单侧杵状指的鉴别诊断流程图

【119】图10-2　双侧杵状指的鉴别诊断流程图

【120】临床上常出现杵状指的疾病包括：呼吸系统疾病如慢性肺脓肿、支气管扩张症、肺间质纤维化以及支气管肺癌等；心血管疾病如发绀型先天性心脏病、亚急性感染性心内膜炎等；消化系统疾病如肝硬化等。

【121】### 一、肺源性肥大性骨关节病

【122】肺源性肥大性骨关节病，又称为增生性肺骨关节病（hypertrophy pulmonary osteoarthropathy，或pulmonary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy，PHOA）是指原发于胸腔内尤其是肺部疾患所伴发的骨关节病变，临床主要表现为杵状指（趾），长骨骨膜增生和骨赘形成以及关节炎。本病约90%继发于各种胸腔内恶性肿瘤，其中80%继发于肺癌，尤其是非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC），此外还见于弥漫性肺间质纤维化、肺脓肿、囊性纤维化、肺结核、支气管扩张症以及慢性阻塞性肺疾病等呼吸系统疾病。PHOA可作为肺癌的首发症状出现，文献报道约30%的肺癌可以伴发杵状指，其中女性较男性多见，所合并的杵状指与其他慢性肺部疾患并发者有一定差异，主要特点是甲床发绀不明显，常常伴有明显的疼痛感，病情进展明显更快，以及甲床周围绕有红晕。关节炎多累及大关节如踝或膝等，表现为局部深在灼痛，夜间明显伴压痛感，可以出现活动受限，X线检查表现为长骨远端的骨膜增生。肺癌切除或治疗后，症状可以缓解，但肿瘤复发时可再次出现。有文献报道，在肺癌的临床特征中，杵状指用于诊断肺癌的阳性似然比约为3.9。具体的发病机制不清楚，有研究认为可能与肿瘤异位分泌生长激素、生长激素释放因子有关。肺部继发性肿瘤患者同样可以伴发PHOA，表现与原发性肺癌相关者类似。囊性肺纤维化、肺间质纤维化、肺脓肿、肺结核等疾病也是常见的导致杵状指的病因，此类疾病往往首先引起肺部通气、换气功能障碍，肺毛细血管氧饱和度降低，低氧血症，进而引起发绀和杵状指。病程发展与原发疾病相关，多数进展缓慢且较难以逆转。

【123】### 二、心血管疾患所致杵状指

【124】伴发于心血管疾患的杵状指多见于发绀型先天性心脏病，如法洛四联症、法洛三联症、大动脉转位以及爱勃斯坦综合征等，同时可出现中心性心源性发绀，艾森曼格综合征患者在并发发绀后也可以逐步出现杵状指。除了心内分流可引起手指（趾）杵状改变以外，肺内分流如肺动静脉瘘也可以导致同样的病变。

【125】感染性心内膜炎（infective endocarditis，IE）也是导致杵状指的常见病因。虽然随着医学技术的进步和疾病谱的变化，IE的病因和临床表现都有了一定的变化，但在发展中国家，风湿性心脏病仍然是IE最为常见的病因，而各种心血管介入检查和治疗技术、血管内及腔内内镜检查等诊断技术、人工瓣膜和血管置换术以及其他心内直视手术的开展，使医源性IE也日益常见和重要。杵状指目前仍然是IE常见的体征之一，文献报道其发病率从29.8%到58.1%不等。IE导致杵状指的发病机制目前尚不清楚。

【126】### 三、消化系统疾患伴发的杵状指

【127】#### （一）肝脏疾病

【128】各种肝脏疾病均可伴发杵状指，其中以肝硬化和肝脏肿瘤最为常见。文献报道，约25%的肝硬化患者可伴发杵状指和发绀。肝脏疾病患者发生杵状指的原因可能与肝肺综合征，肺内分流形成和严重低氧血症有关。肝肺综合征（hepatopulmonary syndrome）以肺血管的明显扩张为病理生理基础。肺功能检查显示肺内分流增加及弥散功能障碍，而肺容量和通气功能多正常。心脏声学造影检查是筛选和确诊肝肺综合征的主要无创检查手段， 99m Tc-MMA动态肺灌注显像也是诊断本病无创而可靠的检查手段，同时也有助于鉴别肺内分流和心内分流。而有创的肺血管造影是诊断本病的金标准，不但可排除肺血栓性疾病，明确诊断，同时可确定肝肺综合征的类型、部位和程度。肝肺综合征是慢性肝病预后不良的独立危险因素，严重肝肺综合征患者即使进行肝移植其术后死亡率也较无肝肺综合征者为高。对于无慢性心肺疾患，原因不明的发绀、杵状指患者，如果同时存在肝病或者肝功能不全时，应注意排除本病。

【129】#### （二）炎性肠病

【130】炎性肠病（inflammatory bowel disease，IBD）包括溃疡性结肠炎和克罗恩病。克罗恩病多从青年时期慢性起病，渐进性发展，表现为腹泻、右下腹痛、腹部包块及发热、呕吐以及消瘦等。40%以上的患者具有不同程度的肠梗阻，肠外表现多变。溃疡性结肠炎是原因不明的慢性结肠炎，多累及直肠和远端结肠，以腹泻、脓血便、腹痛以及里急后重为主要症状。IBD病程迁延，症状繁多，伴有多种多样的肠外症状，可累及皮肤、骨骼、肌肉、神经、内分泌系统等。继发于IBD的骨关节损害称为炎性肠病性关节炎，其中杵状指也相当常见，文献报道在克罗恩病并发杵状指的发病率从31.5%到58%不等，而溃疡性结肠炎患者中有4%～14.5%并发杵状指。且杵状指的出现也被作为IBD病症活跃，预后较差的危险因素。

【149】# 第十一章 胸膜摩擦音/

【150】第十一章　胸膜摩擦音
==========

【151】正常情况下，胸膜腔两层胸膜间的宽度约为10～20μm，内含微量浆液，通常无色、透明，起润滑胸膜作用，从而保证呼吸时脏胸膜和壁胸膜平顺滑动而无声响产生。当各种原因如胸膜纤维素性炎症导致胸膜表面粗糙时，即可随着呼吸运动而出现胸膜摩擦音（pleural friction rub）。

【152】胸膜摩擦音在性质上差别很大，有的声音柔软细微，如丝织物的摩擦声，有的声音很粗糙，如搔抓声、沙沙声、踏雪或握雪的声音，或者似一手掩耳另一手在其手背摩擦时所听到的声音。患者坐位或卧位均可闻及，而以坐位时更加明显，因前下侧胸壁呼吸动度最大而最易听到，肺尖则极少见。胸膜摩擦音在呼吸两相均可听及，十分近耳，在吸气末或者呼气初更加明显，屏气时消失。当深呼吸或听诊器胸件加压时可增强。当胸腔积液较多时，因两层胸膜被分开，则胸膜摩擦音可消失。在胸腔积液吸收过程中当两层胸膜接近时，可再次出现。

【153】# 第十一章 胸膜摩擦音/第一节 病 因

【154】第一节　病　因
-------

【155】凡是可引起胸膜表面粗糙的疾病均有可能出现胸膜摩擦音，因此，可导致胸膜摩擦音的常见病因包括以下几个方面：

【156】##### 1.胸膜炎症

【157】胸膜炎性疾病尤其是发生较多纤维素渗出者易于出现胸膜摩擦音，如纤维素性胸膜炎、结核性胸膜炎、化脓性胸膜炎以及其他原因引起的胸膜炎性疾病。

【158】##### 2.胸膜原发性或继发性肿瘤

【159】见于胸膜间皮瘤和各种胸膜转移性肿瘤。

【160】##### 3.胸膜高度干燥

【161】如严重脱水等。

【162】##### 4.肺部病变累及胸膜

【163】如邻近胸膜的肺炎、肺栓塞等。

【164】##### 5.其他病变

【165】如尿毒症、系统性红斑狼疮等。

【166】# 第十一章 胸膜摩擦音/第二节 发生机制

【167】第二节　发生机制
--------

【168】正常胸膜由于表面光滑，在呼吸过程中尽管脏胸膜和壁胸膜之间存在相互滑动并不产生任何音响。在各种疾病发生在胸膜或累及到胸膜时，由于炎症、肿瘤、纤维素渗出以及胸膜表面病灶等，导致胸膜表面粗糙不平或两层胸膜相互黏附，加之呼吸活动幅度较大时，两层胸膜滑动摩擦阻力加大或两层黏附的胸膜分开，从而出现胸膜摩擦音。鉴于胸膜摩擦音形成的上述机制，在临床上发现，呼吸动度最大的区域易出现胸膜摩擦音，如前下侧胸壁处，而动度较小的区域则很少闻及。

【169】# 第十一章 胸膜摩擦音/第三节 诊断措施

【170】第三节　诊断措施
--------

【171】### 一、病　史

【172】胸膜摩擦音可伴局限性的胸痛，且与呼吸运动相关，并在深呼吸和咳嗽时加重。详细的病史采集有助于胸膜摩擦音病因的鉴别。需了解患者有无胸痛、咳嗽等症状，有无发热、气短以及咯血等其他症状。既往有无关节病变，有无心血管系统和呼吸系统疾患史。近期有无外伤，是否接受过胸腔或心脏手术，有无放疗暴露史。另外需明确患者的吸烟情况。

【173】肺炎患者可有典型的受凉、淋雨或疲劳史，病程上可有上呼吸道感染的前驱症状，多急性起病，伴发热、呼吸困难，可咳嗽、咳铁锈色痰以及胸痛等。有长年吸烟史的中老年男性，出现干咳、间断小量咯血，伴胸痛，发现胸膜摩擦音时要考虑肺癌的可能。而慢性起病患者，低热、盗汗、消瘦，伴或不伴胸痛则要警惕结核性胸膜炎的可能。结缔组织疾病导致的胸膜炎则常见于育龄期女性，可伴关节病变和皮疹。有明确深静脉血栓高危因素如制动史、高凝血状态、口服避孕药等，出现胸痛、胸膜摩擦音、呼吸困难要考虑肺栓塞的可能。

【174】### 二、体格检查

【175】患者除了胸膜摩擦音外还可有呼吸浅快，呼吸音降低，患侧呼吸动度减弱等表现。胸膜摩擦音是单侧还是双侧的，是否伴有下肢水肿或发绀以及杵状指等，患者是否有皮疹、红斑以及关节病变等，均需要仔细检查。

【176】### 三、辅助检查

【177】##### 1.血液学检查

【178】血常规和血生化检查可以了解有无感染血象，有无肾功能、血糖以及血钙等的异常。

【179】##### 2.影像学检查

【180】胸部X线检查是最为重要和基本的检查手段，可显示有无胸腔积液，积液部位、积液量以及有无包裹等，并有助于判断有无肺内病变如肺炎、结核、肺癌，及病变部位等。胸部CT扫描和MRI检查对普通X线检查难以显示的少量胸腔积液具有更好的分辨率，且能通过病灶密度观察将局限包裹性积液与其他病变加以鉴别，还可以在显示胸腔积液同时，更好地了解肺内病变等。

【181】##### 3.病原学检查

【182】如怀疑是感染引发的胸膜病变，并伴发高热，可行血培养；如有胸腔积液，可抽取胸腔积液进行培养；如有痰则行痰涂片和痰培养。

【183】### 四、胸腔积液检查

【184】胸膜摩擦音在渗出性胸膜炎并不是常见体征。超声波和胸部X线检查有助于判断积液量的多少，并协助胸腔穿刺抽液行诊断性检查。所以在胸膜摩擦音较为典型时，胸腔穿刺往往不可进行。如果能获得胸腔积液，则对诊断有较大的帮助。

【185】#### （一）常规检查

【186】##### 1.外观

【187】漏出液常呈清澈、透明的液体，多为淡黄色，静置不凝固，比重＜1.016～1.018。渗出液可因病因不同颜色有所不同，混浊，比重＞1.018。血性胸腔积液可因出血（含红细胞）多少呈淡红血性、洗肉水样、肉眼全血（静脉血样）性。结核性胸腔积液可有草绿色、淡黄色或深黄色、淡红色等。脓性积液则呈黄脓性，厌氧菌感染有恶臭味，阿米巴肝脓肿破入胸腔引起积液呈巧克力色。曲霉或铜绿假单胞菌感染则胸腔积液分别呈黑色和绿色。乳糜胸腔积液呈乳白色，可自凝。

【188】##### 2.细胞计数和分类

【189】漏出液的细胞数较少，有核细胞数常少于100×10 6 /L，以淋巴细胞和间皮细胞为主。渗出液的细胞数较多，有核细胞数常多于500×10 6 /L，以白细胞为主。肺炎伴胸腔积液、脓胸时白细胞数可达10×10 9 /L以上。胸腔积液中红细胞数超过5×10 9 时，胸腔积液可呈淡红色，红细胞数100×10 9 /L以上，呈肉眼血性胸腔积液，主要见于外伤、肿瘤、肺栓塞，但尚需与胸穿损伤所致的血性胸腔积液相鉴别。胸腔积液中以中性粒细胞为主，提示细菌性肺炎、胰腺炎等急性胸膜炎症；结核性胸膜炎或肿瘤所致胸腔积液则以单核细胞为主；嗜酸性粒细胞增多，主要见于寄生虫感染、真菌感染、自发性气胸、结核性胸腔积液反复抽液后、肺梗死、胸部外伤等。恶性胸膜间皮瘤或恶性肿瘤累及胸膜时，胸腔积液中间皮细胞增多，常超过5%。非肿瘤性胸腔积液间皮细胞＜1%。系统性红斑狼疮伴胸腔积液时胸腔积液中可找到狼疮细胞。

【190】#### （二）生化检查

【191】##### 1.pH

【192】结核性胸腔积液、肺炎旁胸腔积液、类风湿性胸腔积液、血胸、脓胸时胸腔积液pH＜7.30，而在脓性胸腔积液、食管破裂所致的胸腔积液下降更显著，甚至pH＜7.0。系统性红斑狼疮及恶性胸腔积液时pH常＞7.35。

【193】##### 2.黏蛋白定性试验（Rivalta试验）

【194】黏蛋白是一种酸性糖蛋白，其等电点为pH 3～5，因此，可在稀醋酸溶液中析出。漏出液黏蛋白含量较少，多为阴性反应；浆膜上皮细胞受炎症刺激分泌黏蛋白量增加，因而渗出液多呈阳性反应。

【195】##### 3.蛋白质

【196】漏出液蛋白含量低，＜30g/L，以白蛋白为主，胸腔积液/血液中蛋白质含量比值＜0.5。渗出液中蛋白＞30g/L，胸腔积液/血液中蛋白质含量比值＞0.5。

【197】##### 4.葡萄糖

【198】正常胸腔积液中葡萄糖含量与血糖相近。漏出液内葡萄糖含量常正常（＞3.35mmol/L）。恶性肿瘤所致的胸腔积液葡萄糖也多正常。由于受细菌或细胞酶的分解，胸腔积液中葡萄糖含量可能下降，主要见于类风湿关节炎并发胸腔积液、结核性胸腔积液、化脓性胸腔积液、少数恶性胸腔积液，而其中脓性胸腔积液和类风湿关节炎并发胸腔积液的葡萄糖可低于1.10mmol/L。

【199】#### （三）酶学测定

【200】##### 1.腺苷脱氨酶（ADA）

【201】当＞45U/L时为升高，结核性胸腔积液ADA常明显升高，可高达100U/L。感染性胸腔积液，如肺炎并发胸腔积液、化脓性胸腔积液等ADA也可升高。肿瘤性胸腔积液ADA通常下降。其他ADA＜45U/L也可见于类风湿关节炎性胸腔积液、SLE并发胸腔积液。

【202】##### 2.乳酸脱氢酶（LDH）

【203】LDH是反映胸膜炎症程度的可靠指标，胸腔积液中LDH含量、胸腔积液LDH/血清LDH的比值有助于判断胸腔积液性质。胸腔积液中LDH含量＞200U/L，胸腔积液LDH/血清LDH的比值＞0.6，则可诊断为渗出液，反之考虑为漏出液。在化脓性胸腔积液或恶性胸腔积液时LDH可明显增高，可达正常血清的10～30倍，其中恶性胸腔积液LDH与患者自身血清中LDH比值达35倍以上。LDH同工酶LDH2增高、LDH4、LDH5降低，提示恶性胸腔积液。而以LDH4、LDH5增高为主，可能为良性胸腔积液。

【204】##### 3.其他

【205】肺癌（主要为小细胞肺癌）胸膜转移并胸腔积液时胸腔积液中神经烯醇化酶（NSE）升高。结核性胸腔积液中血管紧张素转化酶（ACE）明显升高（25U/L）。结核性胸腔积液溶菌酶活性常＞80μg/ml，而恶性胸腔积液溶菌酶活性＜65μg/ml。溶菌酶活性愈高，结核性胸腔积液的可能性愈大。前列腺癌胸膜转移伴胸腔积液酸性磷酸酶升高。急性胰腺炎、食管破裂、恶性肿瘤并发胸腔积液时，胸腔积液淀粉酶可升高。胰腺炎患者约10%可并发胸腔积液，胰腺酶特别是淀粉酶溢出进入胸腔积液中，甚至高于血清淀粉酶水平。

【206】##### 4.肿瘤标志物

【207】癌胚抗原（CEA）及血清糖链肿瘤相关抗原（CA50、CA125、CA199）检查对肿瘤性疾病具有一定的辅助诊断价值。CEA为多种肿瘤相关的标志物，恶性胸腔积液中CEA含量也增高，可作为恶性胸腔积液的鉴别诊断的标志之一。CEA＞10～15μg/L或胸腔积液/血清CEA比值＞1，常提示恶性胸腔积液，而CEA＞20μg/L，胸腔积液/血清CEA＞1诊断恶性胸腔积液的敏感性和特异性均超过90%。胸腔积液CEA对于腺癌尤其是血清中分泌CEA的胃肠道肿瘤、肺腺癌、乳腺癌所致胸腔积液的诊断价值更高。

【208】胸腔积液中CA50水平高于血清，CA50＞20U/ml考虑恶性胸腔积液可能。胸腔积液中CA50、CA199在恶性胸腔积液中升高，敏感性为100%、36%，特异性为10%和96%，对恶性胸腔积液的诊断有一定的参考价值。CEA、CA50、CA125、CA199等联合检测用于恶性胸腔积液的诊断有利于提高敏感性和特异性。

【209】#### （四）免疫学检查

【210】结核性和恶性胸腔积液中淋巴细胞均见升高，前者以CD4 ＋ 辅助淋巴细胞为主（65%±），而后者CD4 ＋ 细胞数量及CD4 ＋ /CD8 ＋ 比值较前者低。

【211】肿瘤性胸腔积液患者的胸腔积液中IL-1 β 、IL-2、sIL-2R、IL-6、IL-8、PDGF、IFN-γ、TNF常下降，且低于结核性胸腔积液。

【212】细菌性肺炎、结核病、癌症、风湿热伴有胸腔积液中类风湿因子滴度常升高达1∶160以上。系统性红斑狼疮、类风湿关节炎性胸腔积液中补体成分（CH50、C3、C4、）降低，相反胸腔积液中免疫复合物含量升高，其胸腔积液含量血清含量比值常大于1。

【213】#### （五）细胞学检查

【214】恶性胸腔积液患者的胸腔积液中检出恶性细胞的几率约为9%～80%，反复多次检查有助于提高检测阳性率，初次阳性率为9%～44%，连续3次以上可提高达80%。此外，恶性肿瘤是否累及或侵犯胸膜、肿瘤组织细胞类型、诊断者技术水平与检出阳性率均密切相关。胸腔积液中细胞染色体数目和形态变异，若以出现10%超二倍体为诊断标准，恶性胸腔积液的确诊率为81%。应用DNA流式细胞分析仪和免疫组织化学分别检出胸腔积液中细胞DNA含量和恶性肿瘤细胞重要相关抗原，用于诊断恶性胸腔积液，与细胞学检查联合应用可显著提高诊断敏感性。

【215】#### （六）病原学检测

【216】采集胸腔积液于无菌试管内，离心沉淀物可行普通细菌、真菌、结核分枝杆菌等培养，沉淀物涂片革兰染色或抗酸染色分别查找普通细菌、真菌、结核分枝杆菌。胸腔积液有时还需行厌氧菌培养、寄生虫如阿米巴原虫和肺吸虫等检测。

【217】#### （七）组织学检查

【218】经皮胸膜活组织检查（简称胸膜活检）对于肿瘤和结核性胸腔积液诊断阳性率约30%～70%。活检大多情况下采用盲检方法，胸腔积液原因不明者均可应用，尤其与胸穿联合使用可提高胸膜炎诊断阳性率。有出血倾向者、脓胸或胸腔积液量甚少时不宜采用。

【219】# 第十一章 胸膜摩擦音/第四节 鉴别诊断

【220】第四节　鉴别诊断
--------

【221】### 一、结核性胸膜炎

【222】结核性胸膜炎（tuberculous pleurisy）是我国最为常见的感染性胸膜炎。其发生机制是结核菌直接感染胸膜和结核菌感染引起的迟发型变态反应。过去认为胸膜炎是结核菌或其代谢产物引起的变态（过敏）反应性炎症。近年来，通过广泛开展的胸腔镜检查和胸膜活检发现，本病患者胸膜多有典型结核性肉芽肿，改变了结核性变态（过敏）反应是本病唯一发病机制的片面观念。结核菌侵入胸膜的途径有：肺门淋巴结结核灶中的结核菌随淋巴逆流至胸膜；肺内结核病灶直接蔓延至胸膜；胸椎或肋骨结核性脓肿溃破入胸膜腔；体内结核病灶中的结核菌血行播散到胸膜。

【223】结核性胸膜炎的临床表现各异，可有结核感染的全身表现如乏力、盗汗、食欲减退、低热、潮热、月经不调；多于患侧有胸膜炎样疼痛、咳嗽、深呼吸时加重，有时还可有胸骨后、肩部、上腹部疼痛；呼吸困难在中等或大量胸腔积液时明显，并常并发压缩性肺不张，由于气管、纵隔向健侧移位也可加重呼吸困难，患者常伴有刺激性干咳。查体时患侧叩浊，呼吸音减低乃至消失，伴有压缩性肺不张时，局部可闻及减低的管状呼吸音；中等、大量积液者，支气管、纵隔向健侧移位。发病早期或吸收期可闻及胸膜摩擦音。

【224】诊断本病时患者可有结核接触史，典型的症状和体征，PPD皮试强阳性，胸腔积液检查发现结核感染依据，如患者有痰，痰中查及抗酸杆菌，抗结核治疗有效。

【225】### 二、肺炎所致胸膜炎

【226】肺炎累及胸膜可导致局部浸润、渗出，形成肺炎旁胸腔积液，重者可致化脓性胸膜炎。8种细菌性肺炎常并发胸腔积液，如肺炎链球菌肺炎、葡萄球菌肺炎、流感嗜血杆菌肺炎、肺炎克雷伯杆菌肺炎、大肠杆菌肺炎、铜绿假单胞菌肺炎、厌氧菌肺炎、军团菌肺炎等，故临床上肺炎旁胸腔积液较常见。约60%的脓胸由肺炎旁胸腔积液发展而来，约5%的肺炎旁胸腔积液患者发展为严重的胸腔细菌性感染，影响疾病的预后。发病以儿童、少年多见，男性多于女性，多伴有营养不良等疾病，冬春季节多发。临床表现上患者有发热、咳脓痰、气促、胸痛及胸部叩浊，呼吸音减弱和消失等体征。血常规多呈感染血象，可见中性粒细胞明显增高，核左移。其胸腔积液的临床特点：①多在细菌性肺炎、肺脓肿、支气管扩张症感染的基础上并发；②胸腔积液外观呈黄色、浑浊；③胸腔积液pH＜7.2，葡萄糖浓度＜2.24mmol/ L，LDH＞1000IU/L；④胸腔积液白细胞计数为（1～91）×10 9 / L，分类以中性粒细胞增高为主。若白细胞总数大于10×10 9 / L，则提示脓胸；⑤细菌性脓胸ADA在45U/L左右或稍高，而结核性脓胸ADA常＞100U/L；⑥胸腔积液涂片或培养可找到致病菌；⑦抗菌治疗，临床症状明显改善。

【227】### 三、病毒性胸膜炎

【228】病毒性胸膜炎（viral pleurisy）约占胸膜炎的5%。多发生于有免疫功能缺陷或服用免疫抑制剂者，亦可见于成人免疫功能低下时。能引起病毒性胸膜炎的病毒有多种，如柯萨奇病毒、埃可病毒、EB病毒、腺病毒、疱疹病毒、肝炎病毒等。起病前多有鼻塞、咽痛等上呼吸道感染症状，胸痛、发热伴气喘为其典型症状。查体可见胸壁的触痛和叩痛，约35%的患者可闻及胸膜摩擦音。起病急骤，全身状况比较好。血沉升高，白细胞计数无明显改变。患者胸腔积液可迅速发生包裹，胸膜增厚粘连，难以进行胸穿抽液，且多在2周内自行吸收。胸腔积液性质为渗出液，以单核细胞为主，蛋白含量高于3.5g/L，糖含量接近血糖水平。胸腔积液PCR检查可查出病毒，血中可能查到病毒特异性抗体。本病病程多不超过4周，为自限性，常被忽略或漏诊。

【229】### 四、肿瘤性胸膜炎

【230】肿瘤累及胸膜局部可能导致胸膜摩擦音，而胸腔积液是更加常见的表现。肿瘤性胸腔积液的准确病因发生率，因研究者不同而报道的百分比有一定差别。肺癌、乳腺癌、淋巴瘤是恶性胸腔积液最常见的三大原因，约占恶性胸腔积液的75%。其具体发生机制包括从胸膜受累到胸膜淋巴管受压，回流受阻，上腔静脉阻塞等。临床表现包括肿瘤本身的表现和胸膜炎表现。肺癌所致胸膜炎患者多为有长年吸烟史的中老年男性，出现咳嗽和间断咯血、胸痛症状，既往可能有呼吸系统基础疾病如肺结核，或者可能有相关危险因素暴露史。胸片、CT等影像学检查和痰细胞学有助于诊断。乳腺癌患者以中年女性多见，可有乳房包块，胸内转移最为常见，起初可为胸部疼痛，以吸气为著；晚期出现胸腔积液时，可出现气促、呼吸困难、咳嗽、咯血等症状，呼吸运动度减低、气管向对侧移位、胸部叩诊呈浊音、呼吸音减低等体征。胸膜摩擦音对乳腺癌胸内转移有提示作用。约有9%的恶性胸腔积液由淋巴瘤引起。胸腔积液可为单侧或双侧。淋巴瘤胸部病变包括原发性肺淋巴瘤和全身淋巴瘤的肺部侵犯。原发性肺淋巴瘤比较少见，所占比例不足1%。临床上以进行性、无痛性淋巴结肿大为主要表现，对肺实质、胸膜的直接侵犯和淋巴结肿大压迫可引起一系列呼吸道症状，如干咳、胸痛、胸闷、气促、发热、咯血、呼吸困难等。胸膜摩擦音对提示淋巴瘤肺病变有一定意义。

【231】### 五、石棉暴露致胸膜病变

【232】长期的石棉暴露和接触史可导致肺间质和胸膜病变，并使肺和胸膜恶性肿瘤发生率明显增高。石棉暴露导致胸膜病变的表现和程度与暴露的时间和接触量相关。非职业性间接接触如石棉工人家属或石棉矿周围居民也可致病。胸膜病变可为胸膜炎，胸腔积液，胸膜纤维化或胸膜恶性病变。石棉接触导致的胸腔积液，其症状变化很大，可无症状，也可有发热、呼吸困难、胸闷、胸痛。积液多为单侧，也可为双侧，左侧多见，为渗出液，有时呈血性。患者可有血沉增高。早期多无明显体征，随着病程进展可有杵状指、发绀、胸膜摩擦音、心肺功能衰竭等体征。胸膜纤维化是石棉所致胸膜病变最为主要的类型，可表现

【87】Diagnosis of a bone lesion as originating from cartilage is usually a simple task for the radiologist. The lesion’s

【88】radiolucent matrix， scalloped margin， and annular， punctate， or comma-shaped calcifications usually suf-fice to establish its chondrogenic nature (Fig. 3-1). However， whether a cartilage tumor is benign or malig-nant is sometimes extremely difficult for the radiologist and the pathologist to determine (33，49，62，70).

【89】All cartilage tumors， whether benign or malignant， exhibit a positive reaction for S-100 protein (54). This is sometimes diagnostically useful， as most other bone tumors do not display this reaction. Histologically， carti-lage tumors are usually recognized by the features of their intercellular matrix， which has a uniformly translu-cent appearance and contains less collagen compared with the intercellular matrix of osteoblastic tumors， such as osteoblastoma and osteosarcoma. The tumor cells themselves are usually located in rounded spaces (lacu-nae)， as in normal cartilage. In benign cartilage tumors， such as enchondroma， the tissue is sparsely cellular (Fig.3-2). The cells， typically with small， dark-staining nuclei， fail to show the cytologic features that are characteristic of chondrosarcoma， such as large nuclei； pleomor-phism；large， swollen chondroblastic and double nuclei； and mitoses. The tumor tissue is usually avascular， and areas of degenerate and calcified matrix are common. Calcification is sometimes followed by vascularization and replacement by bone， as in normal endochondral ossification. Because of their slow growth， enchondro-mas erode and expand the overlying cortical bone (Fig.3-3) but do not invade it， unlike chondrosarcomas. Nevertheless， some slow-growing， low-grade chondrosar-

【92】comas can masquerade as enchondromas， and some aggressive-looking benign cartilage lesions may be mis-takenly diagnosed as chondrosarcomas. Moreover， it is important to be aware of the capricious biological behav- _1or_ ior displayed by cartilage tumors. Some benign-appear-ing lesions of cartilage may behave in an aggressive or malignant manner， whereas tumors that present an omi-nous appearance on radiologic or histologic examina-tion may show limited progression.

【93】Clinically， malignancy is suggested by a variety of signs， including development of pain in a previously asymptomatic lesion (e.g.， malignant transtormation of enchondroma to chondrosarcoma)， development of swelling or a mass at the site of a lesion， or rapid growth of a lesion (e.g.， malignant transformation of osteochon-droma to chondrosarcoma). Radiologically， the pres-ence of a periosteal reaction， destruction of the cortex， and a soft tissue mass are almost pathognomonic fea-tures of malignancy (25). The histopathologic features of a malignant cartilage tumor include the presence of hypercellular and pleomorphic tumor tissue， apprecia-ble numbers of plump cells with large or double nuclei， invasion (permeation) of bone trabeculae， and infiltra-tion of Haversian systems and bone marrow (Fig. 3-4). However， these obvious features of malignancy may be not so prominent in biopsy specimen， or only a few areas in such a specimen may reveal the diagnostic features of malignancy. As Dahlin and Unni (13) pointed out， in the pathologic evaluation it is necessary to examine many fields in these tumors to be certain that there is sufficient evidence for a diagnosis of malignancy be-cause evidence that a tumor is a chondrosarcoma rather than a benign enchondroma is frequently found in iso-lated areas within the mass. Therefore， it is of para-mount importance to obtain biopsy specimens from several areas of a tumor. Close cooperation among the clinician， the radiologist， and the pathologist in review-ing the history， the radiologic examination， and the biopsy specimens is crucial to reaching a conclusion on the exact nature of a cartilage lesion.

【97】2\. Distinguishing a benign cartilage tumor from a malignant one (e.g.， enchondroma from low-grade chondrosarcoma； osteochondroma from exostotic chondrosarcoma； periosteal chondroma from periosteal chondrosarcoma； orsynovial chondromatosis from synovial chondrosarcoma).

【99】From the histopathologic standpoint，because the mi-croscopic features of cartilage lesions are obvious and characteristic， focus should be directed to the following：

【100】1\. Recognition of the varieties of benign cartilage tu-mors (e.g.， enchondroma， periosteal chondroma， chondroblastoma， chondromyxoid fibroma) and various subtypes of chondrosarcoma (e.g.， clear cell， mesenchymal， or periosteal).

【101】2\. Recognition of benign versus malignant tumor(e.g.， enchondroma vs. well-differentiated chon-drosarcoma； chondromyxoid fibroma vs. myxoid chondrosarcoma； or chondroblastoma vs. mes-enchymal chondrosarcoma).

【102】**3\. Differentiation of chondrosarcoma from other malignant tumors that contain cartilage (e.g. from chondroblastic osteosarcoma or periosteal osteosarcoma).**

【103】Benign Lesions

【104】**Enchondroma**

【105】Enchondroma is the second most common benign tu-mor of bone and is characterized by the formation of mature hyaline cartilage. It constitutes about 10% of all benign bone tumors and represents the most common tumor of the phalanges of the hand. Several theories have been postulated regarding its etiology. Among these is that the enchondroma develops from abnor-mal zones of dysplastic chondrocytes in the growth plate. These abnormal foci fail to undergo normal en-dochondral ossification； instead， they are deposited within the metaphysis and， as the bone grows， are dis-placed into the diaphysis (49). Customarily， a lesion lo-cated centrally in the bone is called an enchondroma， whereas one located outside the cortex is called a chon-droma (periosteal or juxtacortical). Separate groups

【106】consist of lesions (a) located in the soft tissues and (b) located in the joint， bursa， or in the tendon sheath. The former are called soft tissue chondromas and the latter synovial chondromatosis (69)

【107】**_Clinical Presentation_**

【108】Although the tumor may occur at any age， most cases arise between the second and fourth decades； there is no sex predilection. The short， tubular bones of the hand and foot (phalanges， metacarpals， and metatarsals) are preferred sites， followed in frequency by the femur， humerus， tibia， and ribs (Fig. 3-5). The lesion is often asymptomatic and usually is discovered incidentally due to a pathologic fracture through the tumor.

【109】The single most important complication of the le-sion is malignant transformation to chondrosarcoma. In a solitary enchondroma this occurs predominantly in a long or flat bone and almost never in a short tubu-lar bone. An important clinical sign is development of pain at the site of the lesion in a previously asympto-matic patient and in the absence of a fracture.

【110】**_Imaging_**

【111】Radiography is usually sufficient to demonstrate the le-sion and to establish its chondroid character. In short. tubular bones， the lesion is often entirely radiolucent(Fig. 3-6)， but in long bones it may display visible calcifi-cations(24). This flocculent mineralization usually assumes the form of dots， rings， and arcs， giving a“pop-corn”appearance (Fig. 3-7). If the calcifications are ex-tensive， the lesion is called a calcifying enchondroma(Fig. 3-8). The cortex is usually thinned and expanded in a symmetric， fusiform fashion. The often cloudy or hazy appearance of a lesion provides a clue to its chon-droid composition (18). The lesion can also be recog nized by scalloped inner cortical margins， reflecting the lobular growth pattern of cartilage (Fig. 3-9). Computedtomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (aMnRoIe) ramnaayy ffaurrtthheerr daelineate the tumor and more pre-cisely localize it in the bone (Fig. 3-10). Like most cartilaginous and fibrous lesions， enchondroma exhibits low to inter-mediate signal intensity on Tl-weighted images and high signal intensity on T2-weighted sequences. 【40】Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (eNK/TCL) is an aggressive Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)–associated lymphoma with a very poor prognosis. It commonly presents in the midline face or skin with large ulcerative nodules, may disseminate rapidly to the viscera and lymph nodes, and is complicated by hemophagocytic syndrome and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Alternative terms in the literature include angiocentric T-cell lymphoma, malignant midline reticulosis, lethal midline granuloma, polymorphic reticulosis, and angiocentric immunoproliferative lesion \[ 1 , 2 \]. One extremely important point to note is that this is not a lymphoma of natural killer T cells (NKT cells), but rather a neoplasm of NK cells or cells with a cytotoxic T-cell phenotype. Hence they are termed NK / T-cell lymphomas \[ 1 \]. Some differentiate eNK/TCLs that occur in the aerodigestive tract (nasal eNK/TCL) from those that occur elsewhere (nasal-type), but regardless of the primary site, the histology is identical \[ 1 \]. This chapter discusses the clinical presentation, prognosis, treatment, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, molecular characteristics, and differential diagnosis of eNK/TCL. The chapter closes with a clinical case featuring a patient with eNK/TCL arising in the nose with subsequent cutaneous involvement.

【41】9.1 Clinical
------------

【42】### 9.1.1 Clinical Presentation

【43】Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphomas, nasal type (eNK/TCL) are aggressive, angioinvasive, angiodestructive, necrotizing lymphomas that can cause extensive tissue destruction and have an extremely poor prognosis \[ 1 , 2 \]. eNK/TCL is far more common in East Asians \[ 3 \] and in patients of Native American descent East Mexico and Central and South America (particularly from Peru) \[ 4 , 5 \]. eNK/TCL accounts for 1.5 % of all lymphomas in the United States and 3.3–8 % of lymphomas in East Asia \[ 6 \]. This form of lymphoma is more common in adults and is two to three times more common in men than in women \[ 1 , 7 \]. The mean age of onset is 44 years \[ 8 \].

【44】eNK/TCL is strongly associated with the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) \[ 1 , 7 , 9 \]. Although the role of EBV in eNK/TCL pathogenesis is poorly understood, it is thought that East Asians are more likely to develop this lymphoma because of the higher prevalence of EBV in East Asian populations \[ 7 , 8 , 10 \].

【45】Nasal eNK/TCL arises in the mucosa of the aerodigestive tract, and typically presents as ulcerative nodules in the midline of the face; these lesions can result in dramatic facial destruction. Other associated findings may include nasal obstruction, epistaxis, nasal discharge, purulent rhinorrhea, proptosis, extraocular muscle restriction, oronasal fistulas, and facial edema \[ 1 , 2 , 7 , 9 \]. eNK/TCL occurring at extranasal sites (nasal-type eNK/TCL) has identical histopathology, phenotype, and genotype \[ 2 \]. Approximately 10 % of cases of nasal-type eNK/TCL arise primarily in the skin; these tend to be disseminated at presentation \[ 2 , 6 \]. Cutaneous manifestations typically include numerous, painful, generalized, ulcerated nodules on the trunk and extremities \[ 1 , 11 \] (Fig. 9.1 ). Patients generally present with localized disease (76 %) at diagnosis and tend to have good performance status, normal lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) (63 %), and lack B symptoms (35 %) \[ 12 \]. Other common primary sites of eNK/TCL include the testis and gastrointestinal tract \[ 2 , 6 \].

【48】Lymph node involvement can occur secondarily in eNK/TCL, but bone marrow involvement is rare \[ 13 \]. Patients with eNK/TCL can experience rapid spread to the gastrointestinal tract, testes, cervical lymph nodes, lungs, liver, brain, and rarely the eye or orbit \[ 1 , 7 , 8 , 13 – 15 \]. Once the lymphoma spreads beyond the skin, patients often develop fever, hemophagocytic syndrome, and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) \[ 1 , 6 , 15 \].

【49】### 9.1.2 Prognosis and Treatment

【50】Patients with eNK/TCL have an estimated survival of 6–30 months. The mean 5-year survival rate for eNK/TCL patients ranges from 30 to 50 %, even with treatment \[ 1 , 6 – 8 , 16 \]. Poor prognostic indicators include advanced stage (III or IV), invasion of bone or skin, high levels of EBV DNA in the blood, and detection of EBV in the bone marrow \[ 1 \]. Specific prognostic models for eNK/TCL have been proposed; adverse risk factors included in a model presented by Lee et al. \[ 12 \] include advanced stage, the presence of B symptoms, lymph node involvement, and elevated LDH. In this model, the 5-year overall survival rate was 81 % for patients with none of these risk factors, 64 % with one risk factor, 34 % with two risk factors, and 7 % with three or more \[ 12 \]. Extranasal eNK/TCLs (nasal-type) tend to be even more aggressive than nasal eNK/TCL and are minimally responsive to therapy \[ 1 \]. Circulating EBV DNA released by dead tumor cells can help predict tumor burden and prognosis, and can assist with diagnosis and monitoring \[ 1 , 6 \].

【51】The standard of care for limited-stage disease is multiagent chemotherapy in combination with localized radiation therapy \[ 6 , 7 \]. eNK/TCL is likely to be highly resistant to chemotherapy because of high levels of expression of the multidrug resistance protein (MRP), which pumps some chemotherapeutic agents out of neoplastic cells \[ 6 , 17 \]. Although allogeneic stem cell transplantation has been effective in a handful of patients, patients who relapse after transplant have a markedly poor outcome \[ 7 \]. Studies have reported excellent responses to high-dose radiation therapy \[ 18 \], and several promising chemotherapy regimens are under investigation \[ 19 – 22 \].

【52】9.2 Pathology
-------------

【53】### 9.2.1 Histopathology

【54】Although eNK/TCLs may be differentiated based on primary site (nasal vs nasal-type) the histopathology is identical \[ 1 \].

【55】Skin biopsy shows a diffuse dermal infiltrate of neoplastic NK/T cells \[ 1 , 7 – 10 \]. The overlying epidermis or mucosa typically shows extensive ulceration and loss of mucosal glands. Alternatively, marked pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia of the above epithelium can occur \[ 1 \].

【56】Prominent angiocentricity and angiodestruction is the hallmark of this lymphoma \[ 1 , 7 – 10 \] (Figs. 9.2 and 9.3 ). Necrosis and apoptosis may occur secondary to vascular occlusion and the release of cytokines or chemokines by neoplastic cells \[ 1 \] (Fig. 9.4 ). Because these tumors are often associated with marked necrosis, a large biopsy sample is often needed to ensure that viable tumor is present and that key findings such as angiocentricity are not missed \[ 6 , 7 , 23 \].

【63】The neoplastic NK/T-cell infiltrate is typically composed of medium-sized cells or a mixture of small and large cells, which are occasionally anaplastic. The tumor cells have a moderate amount of pale-to-clear cytoplasm and characteristic irregularly folded and elongated nuclei; they have thus been deemed “cucumber cells.” The tumor cells may demonstrate small, inconspicuous nucleoli and granular or vesicular chromatin; cytoplasmic azurophilic granules are visible on Giemsa stain \[ 1 , 6 \]. A dense, inflammatory infiltrate of small lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, and eosinophils may also be present \[ 1 \].

【64】### 9.2.2 Immunophenotype and Molecular Findings

【65】The neoplastic NK cells are positive for CD56, CD2, cytoplasmic CD3epsilon, CD45RO, HLA-DR, CD25, FAS/CD95, and FAS ligand \[ 1 , 9 , 10 \] (Table 9.1 ). The cells frequently express cytotoxic molecules including granzyme B, TIA-1, and perforin \[ 1 , 10 \]. The tumor cells are generally negative for surface CD3, CD4, CD5, CD8, TCR delta, betaF1, and CD57, and only occasionally express CD7 or CD30 \[ 1 \]. Rare cases derived purely from cytotoxic T cells show a similar immunophenotype, but may express CD8 and surface CD3 (Fig. 9.5 ).

Importantly, because only one third to one half of cases demonstrate expression of the EBV protein LMP-1, this test not an appropriate surrogate for EBV detection \[ 10 \].

【75】9.3 Differential Diagnosis
--------------------------

【76】### 9.3.1 Diagnostic Considerations

【77】Diagnosis requires an integration of clinical, immunologic, and genetic data. Midline location can be a key diagnostic feature for eNK/TCLs on the face. Immunohistochemical stains characteristically demonstrate at least one NK-cell marker (CD56, CD16, or CD57) without surface CD3 expression. B-cell markers (CD19 and CD20) or myeloperoxidase (MPO) should not be expressed. These tumors are EBV positive. Unlike many other lymphomas, the T-cell receptor and immunoglobulin genes are typically in their germ-line configuration \[ 1 , 2 , 9 \], with the exception of rare cases of cytotoxic T-cell lineage, which may demonstrate clonal T-cell receptor rearrangements (see Fig. 9.5 ).

【78】### 9.3.2 Differential Diagnosis

【79】#### 9.3.2.1 Hydroa Vacciniforme-Like Lymphoma (HVLL)

【80】HVLL is a rare, EBV-positive, aggressive cutaneous T-cell lymphoma characterized by angioinvasion and angiodestruction. It generally occurs in children from Latin America or Asia. It can present as ulcerated nodules with scarring, a vesicopapular skin eruption resembling hydroa vacciniforme, and/or edema of the lips and periorbital region \[ 25 \]. Immunophenotyping helps in achieving the correct diagnosis: HVLL typically lacks CD56 expression, whereas eNK/TCL is CD56+ \[ 11 \].

【81】#### 9.3.2.2 Lymphomatoid Granulomatosis (LyG)

【82】LyG is an angiocentric, angiodestructive, EBV-associated B-cell lymphoma that nearly always involves the lungs. Cutaneous involvement occurs in approximately half of patients, with a variable presentation that ranges from ulcerated subcutaneous and dermal nodules to violaceous, maculopapular eruptions \[ 26 \]. One of the key differentiating features is that LyG is a B-cell lymphoproliferative disease; eNK/TCL is not. Although eNK/TCL is much more common in East Asian populations, LyG shows no such ethnic predilection but often occurs in the setting of immunosuppression \[ 2 \].

【83】#### 9.3.2.3 CD8+ Aggressive Epidermotropic Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma (AECTCL)

【84】In the setting of angioinvasion/angiodestruction and rapid onset of ulcerative nodules, CD8+ AECTCL is a diagnostic consideration. Immunohistochemical stains are usually helpful in this differential diagnosis: CD8+ AECTCL manifests as an epidermotropic infiltrate of CD8+ T cells, but the tumor cells in eNK/TCL are usually negative for CD8. eNK/TCL is associated with EBV; CD8+ AECTCL is not \[ 1 , 27 \].

【85】#### 9.3.2.4 Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm (BPDCN)

【86】Given the CD56 positivity of the atypical cells and the presence of TCR in the germline configuration, BPDCN may be considered in the differential diagnosis of eNK/TCL \[ 9 \]. This tumor is derived from blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cells rather than from mature NK cells, as is eNK/TCL. The neoplastic blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cells of BPDCN are EBV negative, lack cytoplasmic granules, and are strongly positive for CD4 and CD123, which are not expressed in eNK/TCL \[ 9 \]. BPDCN also lacks the angiocentricity and angiodestruction characteristic of eNK/TCL \[ 28 \].

【87】#### 9.3.2.5 Pyoderma Gangrenosum (PG)

【88】When eNK/TCL occurs at sites other than the face, the clinical differential diagnosis may include PG. Characterized by large, ulcerated lesions, PG may clinically resemble eNK/TCL, but PG is a neutrophilic dermatosis featuring prominent edema and a dense neutrophilic infiltrate, in contrast to the NK/T-cell infiltrate of eNK/TCLs. The EBV positivity, angiocentricity, and angiodestruction characteristic of eNK/TCL are absent in PG \[ 29 \].

【89】9.4 Clinical Case
-----------------

【90】Case 9.1

【91】A 39-year-old immigrant from Southeast Asia with a history of EBV-positive nasal extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma presented with a 1-month history of approximately 15 new, painful, rapidly enlarging, violaceous subcutaneous nodules on his calf, measuring 1–3 cm (see Fig. 9.1 ). His nasal NK/T-cell lymphoma was diagnosed 4 years ago, after 2 years of facial pain, drainage, eyelid ptosis, and nasal obstruction. At that time, he had no evidence of hemophagocytic syndrome or systemic involvement. Treatment with high-dose radiation therapy initially led to clearance of the lesions and complete remission for nearly 2 years. His radiation therapy was complicated by severe radiation dermatitis, mucositis, esophagitis, and thrush. His recovery was further complicated by repeated necrotizing pneumonias.

【1】cinoma group 73% relapsed and 55% died of disease. Adverse prognosticfactors include extrathyroidal extension， nodal metas-tases， and positive marg in at surgery and solid growth pattern. Of these extrathyroidal extension and nodal metastases are inde-pendent predictors of prognosis on multivariate analyses \[293\].

【2】_Differential Diagnosis_ The diagnosis of oncocytic neo-plasm in most cases is made by the distinetive oncocytic nature of the cells. Evaluation of the tumor capsule is needed to dis-tinguish adenoma from carcinoma， as mentioned earlier in the case of follicular carcinoma. In the case of carcinoma， lesions that sometimes may have to distinguished include oncocytic variant of medullary carcinoma and parathyroid oxyphil tumor. If the tumor shows extensive clear cell change， it should be dis-tinguished from other clear cell tumors such as metastatic renal cell carcinoma and clear cell medullary carcinoma. For medul-lary carcinoma， the presence of amyloid and positive immuno-histochemical staining with chromogranin， calcitonin， calci-tonin-gene-related peptide， and CEA are helpful.

【3】PAPILLARY ONCOCYTIC NEOPLASMS Oncocytic tumors may sometimes exhibitapredominantly papillary architecture com-prised of papillae without awell-developed fibrovascular core. These tumors are designated as oncocytic papillary neoplasms and should be distinguished from oncocytic papillary thyroid carcinomas based on the characteristic nuclear changes of pap-illary carcinoma \[132\].

【4】_Poorly Differentiated Carcinoma_ Differentiated thyroid carcinoma of both papillary and follicular type may progress to a more poorly differentiated phenotype. This poorly differen-tiated carcinoma may present as a more distinet morphologic entity referred to as insular carcinoma or a group of less-well-defined morphologic phenotype. The latter group of poorly dif-ferentiated thyroidcarcinoma， which has included entities such as columnar and tall variants of papillary carcinoma and tumors with solid and trabecular architecture， has been controversial. with its inclusion as a distinct category in question \[300\].

【5】INSULAR CARCINOMA Insular carcinoma is a morphologi-cally distinct form of tumor derived from the thyroid follicular cells having an aggressive biological course. The incidence of these tumors varies from being rare in the United States to about4% of all thyroid cancers seen in an Italian study \[132\]. We have ourselves seen several cases of pure insular carcinoma in our practice， and it is not uncommon to see foci of insular growth associated with differentiated thyroid tumorsin someother cases(personal experience). These tumors tend to involve elderly patients with a slight female predilection \[132\].

【6】On gross examination these tumors are large in size and ex-hibit an invasive growth with associated areas of necrosis (Fig.12A). On histology they are composed of well-defined islands of round or oval cells that lack significantpleomorphism. Small microfollicular structures may be seen within these islands， and it is notuncommon to see necrosis in the center of these islands(Fig. 12B). Foci of vascularinvasion are notinfrequent\[30，132\].

【7】_Differential Diagnosis_ The tumor that insular carcinoma should be differentiated from and can pose problems on mor-phology is medullary carcinoma.Immunohistochemistry is very useful in these situations. Insular carcinoma cells are positive for thyroglobulin and negative for calcitonin and other neuro-endocrine markers. Another primary tumor that may have to be

【9】differentiated is the solid variant of papillary carcinoma， which is more common following exposure to nuclear radiation \[270，271\]. In these cases the nuclear features of papillary carcinoma are helpful in differential diagnosis.

【10】_Anaplastic Carcinoma_ Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is a highly aggressive and rare thyroid tumor， accounting for 1.7%of all thyroid cancers in the United States \[165\]. Its incidence is higher in regions endemic for goiter \[301\]. The patients are usually elderly in their seventh or eight decade of life， with a female preponderance of approx 2.5：1 \[165\]. A personal his-tory of goiter may be seen in approx 25% of cases and prior exposure to radiation in 9.4% cases \[165\].Patients present with rapidly enlarging neck mass associated with compressingsymp-toms such as dysphagia， hoarseness， and stridor. Often signs and symptoms related to metastatic tumor may be the first pre-sentation \[132，165\]. On gross examination the tumor is usually large， the majority being >4.0 cm \[165\]， often replacing the entire thyroid and spreading into the perithyroidal soft tissues\[132\].On microscopic examination， the tumor may exhibit one of the three patterns or a mixture of more than one of these pat-terns including squamoid pattern resembling the nonkeratiniz-ing squamous cell carcinoma， spindle cell pattern resembling sarcoma， and giant cell type (Fig. 13B). All three types of pat-tern are associated with a high mitotic rate and focal necrosis may be seen. The spindle cell sarcomalike pattern may show paucicellular areas with dense fibrosis that may alternate with cellular areas， which aids in the diagnosis of anaplastic thyroid carcinoma \[30，132\]. The giant cell pattern is associated with a marked degree of pleomorphism with large multinucleated cells including tumor giant cells. The tumors are highly inva-sive with infiltration of the perithyroidal soft tissues \[132\]. In some cases heterologous stromal elements including cartilage or bone may be seen \[132\].

【11】On immunohistochemistry the squamoid-type tumors are positive for high-and low-molecular-weight keratin，EMA， and sometimes CEA. The spindle cell pattern shows variable posi-tivity with low-molecular-weight keratin ranging in incidence from 47% to 100% cases. Thyroglobulin staining is also vari-able， ranging from 9% to 71% cases and is usually focal and weak \[132\]. Ultrastructurally evidence of epithelial differenti-ation is seen in most tumors \[1321.

【12】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF ANAPLASTIC CARCINOMA Thesqua-moid type anaplastic carcinoma should be differentiated from metastatic carcinoma from primary sites such as lung，esopha-gus，and upper aerodigestive tract. The history of arapidly grow-ing mass in the region of the thyroid together with the finding of differentiated thyroid carcinoma in some areas and positive immunostaining with thyroglobulin may be helpful in the dif-ferential diagnosis.

【13】The spindle-cell-type tumor should be differentiated from _true sarcoma such as fibrosarcoma， malignant fibrous histio-cytoma， angiosarcoma， and hemangiopericytoma. This may_ pose the greatest difficulty especially in cases where the entire tumor is of spindle cell type and is paucicellular. Features that favor anaplastic thyroid carcinoma include foci of better-dif-ferentiated areas， justifying thorough sampling of the tumor and evidence of epithelial differentiation on immunohis-tochemistry and electron microscopy. In addition， metaplastic spindle cell proliferation， which can sometimes be seen asso-ciated with papillary carcinoma and follicular adenoma \[183\]， should also be differentiated from spindle-cell-type anaplastic carcinoma because of the significant difference in the biologi-cal behavior and management of the two entities.

【14】_Medullary thyroid carcinoma may show a variety of growth_ patterns， and this may have to be differentiated from the spindle cell type and pleomorphic variants of anaplastic carcinoma.

【15】**Figure 13 Anaplastic carcinoma. (A) Giant cell type with necrosis； (B) spindle cell type.**

【16】Immunohistochemistry plays a very important role in this dif-ferentiation and must be performed using antibodies to calcito-nin， chromogranin， and CEA， which are all positive in medullary carcinoma \[132\].

【17】Malignant lymphoma may also be considered in cases with small cells； however， the even distribution of smaller， uniform cells in lymphoma and lack of focal epithelial islands is helpful in this differential diagnosis \[132\].

【18】Riedel's thyroiditis may be confused with the paucicellular spindle-cell-typeanaplastic thyroid carcinoma， which may show marked sclerosis and lack significant pleomorphism and mito-tic activity. In these cases， features that favor anaplastic carci-noma include the presence of necrosis， more cellular areas，and evidence of vascular invasion and metastases \[30\]. The more cellular areas and better differentiated thyroid carcinoma may be seen on extensive sampling，whichis crucial in the diagnosis of anaplastic carcinoma in these problematic cases.

【19】The prognosis in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is extremely poor， with mean survival of 7.2±10 mo \[132\].

【20】**_Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma_**

【21】CLINICAL FEATURES ANDETIOLOGYThe tumorderived from the thyroid C cells that is now referred to as medullary carcinoma was first regarded as an unusual variant of anaplastic carcinoma\[30\]. The term medullary carcinoma was coined by Hazard et al. in 1959， who reviewed 600 cases of thyroid cancer over a31-yr period at the Cleveland Clinic， reported 21 tumors with unique morphological features including solid growth pattern and amyloid stroma， and called them medullary carcinoma \[302\]. Later Williams in 1966 identified the cell of origin of these tumors as C cells \[3031.Medullary thyroid carcinoma is a rare tumor with a incidence of 3.2%(0.5% familial and 2.7%spora-dic) of all thyroid cancers in acohort of more than 5500 patients in the United States \[165\]. One of the unique features of this tumor is that it occurs both in a familial setting associated other endocrine neoplasms as part of the multiple endocrine neo-

【22】**plasia syndrome (MEN) and also as sporadic tumors in a non-familial setting \[304，305\].**

【23】Sporadic medullary carcinoma is the more common form of tumor， representing approx 80% of all medullary carcinomas. The remaining 20% are familial and are inherited as autosomal dominant trait with high penetrance \[30，165\]. The latter may either occur in association with other endocrine tumors as part ofMEN2A，which includes in addition to medullary carcinoma， adrenal medullary hyperplasia-pheochromocytoma and para-thyroid hyperplasia-adenoma and MEN 2B \[3\]，which includes， in addition to pheochromocytoma， mucosal ganglioneuroma and skeletal abnormalities. In addition these may occur as fa-milial non-MEN medullary thyroid carcinoma \[306-309\].The gene for MEN 2A and 2B syndrome is called the RET proto-oncogene， which is located on chromosome 10. Germline mis-sense mutation of this gene is seen in patients with MEN2A and MEN 2B \[306，307，310-312\]. Sporadic tumors may sometime show mutation in the RET protooncogene \[312\].

【24】The age at presentation in the familial form of medullary carcinoma is younger than in the sporadic form and both show a slight female predilection \[132\]. With increased prospective screening of family members of MEN patients， the age at pres-entation of familial form of medullary carcinoma is becoming progressively younger \[132\]. The sporadic form presents with a solitary mass with or without lymph node metastases. The familial form is usually multicentric and bilateral. In addition， patients may have diarrhea and both carcinoid and Cushing's syndromes have been reported \[132，304，305\].Increased levels of serum calcitonin and CEA are seen in both familial and spora-dicmedullary carcinoma and are important diagnostictests \[132\].

【25】PATHOLOGY OF MEDULLARY CARCINOMA The tumors vary in size from barely visible to large tumors that may replace the entire lobe； the smaller tumors are often seen in patients with MEN 2 syndrome who undergo prophylactic thyroidectomy for high serum calcitonin levels that are discovered at routine

【26】screening. The small tumors， which are <1.0 cm， are referred to as medullary microcarcinoma and are commonly seen at the junction of upper and middle thirds of the lobes \[304，313-315\]. In these cases it is important that the entire gland be submitted so that small tumors that may not be apparent grossly are not missed. On sectioning the tumors have firm yellow white cut surface.Thelarge tumors usually have an indistinct border and most are not encapsulated. However， rarely a thick fibrous capsule may sometimes be seen and may sometimes be associ-ated with cystic and papillary change \[132，316\].

【27】On microscopic examination medullary carcinomas are usu-ally circumscribed and show a variety of growth patterns that may mimic follicular，papillary，insular， and anaplastic thyroid carcinoma， emphasizing the importance of careful morpho-logic evaluation and use of immunostaining to differentiate it from these follicular-cell-derived tumors \[30，132，317\]. The most typical growth pattern includes solid nests or trabeculae or an insular pattern separated with thin fibrovascular core. The cells within these nests are round， oval， or spindle shaped， with a finely granular dispersed chromatin typical of neuroendocrine cells； giant multinucleated cells may sometimes be seen. The cytoplasmis amphophilic or eosinophilic and may appear clear， sometimes with occasional mucin positive intracytoplasmic vacuoles \[132\]. Amyloid (Fig. 14F) may be seen in the stroma in up to 80% of tumors， and stains positively with calcitonin on immunohistochemistry. In the familial type of medullary car-cinoma areas of C-cell hyperplasia are usually seen associated with the tumor， which is a feature not seen in sporadic tumors\[132，296，318\].On immunohistochemistry， the tumor cells are negative for thyroglobulin and positive for panneuroendocrine markers such as synaptophysin and chromogranin， and more specific markers such as calcitonin and calcitonin gene-related peptide. In addition， CEA is another useful marker that is posi-tive in medullary carcinoma \[132，317\]. Sex steroid receptors， especially the progesterone receptor， may be seen in medullary carcinoma on immunohistochemistry \[319\]. Ultrastructurally the characteristic membrane-bound neurosecretory granules are seen in the cytoplasm \[132\].

【28】Medullary carcinoma variants include follicular variant， papillary variant， oncocytic variant (Fig.14E)， small cell vari- _ant， giant cell variant， clear cell variant， melanotic variant，_ _squamous variant， encapsulated variant， and paraganglioma-_ like variant \[132，316，320\]. The presence of all these variants makes medullary carcinoma the great mimicker of other thy-roid carcinoma； therefore immunohistochemistry should be performed in all cases when the diagnosis is in doubt or some atypical features are present.

【29】**The prognosis in medullary carcinoma shows considerable variation. The 5-and 10-yr survival rates are 60-70% and 40-50%， respectively. Better prognostic factors include younger age， females，early tumor stage， and familial tumors \[132，321\].**

【30】**_C-Cell Hyperplasia and Medullary Microcarcinoma_ C-CELL HYPERPLASIA**

【31】_General Considerations_ The calcitonin-producing Ccells are derived from the neural crest and descend down into the thyroid with the ultimobranchial body； therefore，they are found mainly at the junction of the upper and middle third of the two thyroid lobes， frequently associated with solid cell nests \[14\].

【32】C cells are usually visualized on routine hematoxylin and eosin stains but may be easily seen on immunohistochemistry (Fig.14). Theincreasein the numbers of C cells is referred to as C-cell hyperplasia. C-cell hyperplasia， which was first described by Wolfe in 1973 in patients with MEN 2A \[322\]， can also be seen to be associated in certain other situations with no evidence of MEN 2. Whereas the former is referred to as familial C-cell hyperplasia， thought to be a neoplastic proliferation， the latter is called physiological or secondary C-cell hyperplasia \[323，324\].

【33】_The familial C-cell hyperplasia is thought to be neoplastic_ and is regarded as a precursor of familial type of medullary+hatar十carcinoma； therefore the term hyperplasia for these lesions is a misnomer and has been questioned \[323，325\]. It is thought to represent the preinvasive stage (carcinoma in situ) of medul-ISIYE lary carcinoma \[324\]. The neoplastic nature of this form of“hyperplasia”is further supported by the fact that C cells are clonal \[326\] and show a polysialic acid immunostaining pat-tern that is distinct from the physiological/reactive C-cell hyper-plasia \[3271.

【34】_Physiological C-cell hyperplasia， also referred to as reac-_ tive or secondary C-cell hyperplasia， has been associated with conditions causing hypercalcemia such as hyperparathyroid-ism \[328，329\]. This form of C-cell hyperplasia has also been seen associated with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis \[330，331\]， multi-nodular goiter， hyperthyroidism，lymphoma \[332，333\]，around thyroid tumors of follicular cell origin \[334\]， and following subtotal thyroidectomy \[335\].

【35】_Diagnosis_ SThe diagnostic criteria for what constitutes C-cell hyperplasia are not clearly established. It includes defini-tions ranging from imprecise descriptions of C-cell volume， which can be very subjective \[323，336\]， to semiquantatative estimates such as>50 cells per 50 low-power fields to>50 cells per l low-power field \[323\]. Guyent et al. have proposed more precise quantitative criteria that include >40 cells/cm² or>50cells in 3 low-power (×100) fields \[337\]. 【38】HISTORY

【39】A 45-year-old woman with cough, chronic weight loss, and no history of fever.

【40】 FIGURES 1-16A and 1-16B Posteroanterior and lateral chest radiographs. There is homogeneous consolidation in the right middle lobe and, to a lesser extent, the lingula. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy is present. Incidental note is made of nipple markers on the frontal radiograph.

【41】 FIGURE 1-16C Chest CT (lung window) through the lower lungs, obtained several weeks after the radiograph. There is homogeneous consolidation without cavitation throughout the majority of the right middle lobe and portions of the lingula. Air bronchograms are present within the right middle lobe consolidation.

【42】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【43】If the findings are acute and/or resolve on follow-up imaging :

【44】 Pneumonia: Lobar consolidation is usually caused by bacterial infection. Organisms include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Legionella pneu-mophila , gram-negative bacteria, and M. tuberculosis . A bacterial infection is unlikely with a history of chronic weight loss and no fever, although TB or fungal infections (e.g., blastomycosis) can have subacute presentations. As TB or fungal infections such as blastomycosis can cause consolidation that does not resolve with standard antibiotic therapy, they should be differential considerations in this patient.

【45】 Aspiration pneumonia: Aspiration of gram-negative or anaerobic bacteria may cause lobar consolidation. Aspiration most commonly causes scattered, poorly defined consolidation or “tree-in-bud” centrilobular nodules in the dependent segments of lung. Involvement of the anterior portions of the lungs as in this patient would make this diagnosis less likely.

【46】If the findings are chronic and/or do not resolve on follow-up imaging :

【47】 Invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma \[formally known as mucinous bronchioloalveolar cell carcinoma (BAC)\]: The clinical presentation and homogeneous consolidation with air bronchograms could be due to invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma. Since in this case the consolidative opacities failed to resolve on follow-up imaging, this is a strong diagnostic possibility in this patient. A histologic diagnosis, such as from lung biopsy, is necessary to confirm this diagnosis.

【48】 Primary lymphoma of lung: This rare non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma is usually low grade, and patients are often asymptomatic. Consolidation with air bronchograms and poorly defined margins is the most common presentation; therefore, based on the images provided, this is a diagnostic possibility in this patient. Mass-like and reticulonodular opacities are less frequent imaging appearances of this rare disease.

【49】 Alveolar sarcoid: While sarcoid may cause chronic consolidation with air bronchograms, the consolidation is most often nodular in configuration. Large foci of consolidation that occupy the majority of a lobe would be unusual.

【50】 Exogenous lipoid pneumonia: The aspiration of lipid containing material can result in chronic consolidation. On CT, the consolidation often contains foci of fat attenuation. However, the inflammation that results as a result of the aspiration can obscure the fat droplets; therefore, lipoid pneumonia does not always demonstrate fat attenuation on CT. As with other forms of aspiration noted above, the anterior location of the consolidation as seen in this patient would be unusual.

【51】DIAGNOSIS (ON BIOPSY, AFTER CONSOLIDATION FAILED TO RESOLVE)

【52】Invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma

【53】KEY FACTS

【54】Clinical

【55】 Invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma is a subtype of ade-nocarcinoma that contains tumor cells that: have a goblet morphology; contain abundant cytoplasmic mucin; and demonstrate “lepidic” growth, which means that the cells line the alveoli without distorting the underlying lung architecture.

【56】 The 2011 classification of lung adenocarcinoma replaced the term “bronchioloalveolar cell carcinoma,” or BAC, with several different subtypes of adenocarcinoma.

【57】 Invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma was previously known as “mucinous BAC.” This form of adenocarci-noma demonstrates lepidic growth but is usually multifo-cal and may involve one or more entire lobes of the lung.

【58】 The 2011 classification of lung adenocarcinoma replaced the term “nonmucinous BAC” with three different terms. A solitary, focal adenocarcinoma that demonstrates lepidic growth but does not invade the vessels, lymphatics, or pleura is now referred to as “adenocar-cinoma in situ” (AIS). A solitary, focal adenocarcinoma that demonstrates primarily lepidic growth but shows minimal (< 5 mm) invasion of stroma is termed “minimally invasive adenocarcinoma” (MIA). A solitary, focal adenocarcinoma that demonstrates primarily lepidic growth but shows > 5 mm stromal invasion is referred to as “lepidic predominant adenocarcinoma” (LPA).

【59】 Clinical features that distinguish invasive mucinous ade-nocarcinoma from other lung cancers are (1) younger age at presentation, (2) higher incidence in women compared to other forms of lung cancer, (3) copious watery sputum (bronchorrhea), and (4) higher incidence in nonsmokers.

【60】 AIS, MIA, and LPA have an indolent course, with a very high 5-year survival rate. Invasive mucinous adenocar-cinoma, however, behaves more aggressively, and the 5-year survival rate is much lower.

【61】Radiologic

【62】 AIS and MIA present as solitary pulmonary nodules that are purely ground glass in attenuation. These pure ground glass nodules may remain stable over long periods of time or may grow very slowly. Comparison with remote prior studies or follow- up for extended periods of time is warranted to exclude indolent growth.

【63】 LPA presents as a solitary pulmonary nodule that is primarily ground glass in attenuation.

【64】 When nodules that were previously purely ground glass in attenuation acquire a soft tissue component, the change is worrisome for development of invasion.

【65】 Invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma most often presents as consolidation with air bronchograms, and radiologically may resemble pneumonia.

【66】 In patients with chronic consolidation that is concerning for invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma, a search for findings that would suggest metastatic disease (such as adenopa-thy, pleural effusions, or adrenal masses) is warranted.

【73】Asymptomatic 71-year-old man undergoes a routine annual chest radiograph.

【77】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【78】 Hamartoma: This is the best diagnosis because of the presence of fat within the nodule as evident on CT.

【79】 Exogenous lipoid pneumonia: This is a differential consideration given the internal fat density on CT. However, aspiration of lipoid material (such as mineral oil) usually results in an ill-defined focus of consolidation rather than the smoothly marginated nodule, as seen in this patient.

【80】 Tuberculoma: Round noncalcified solitary nodules are an uncommon manifestation of parenchymal TB. They are usually encountered in asymptomatic adults. The majority (75%) occur in the upper lobes, as opposed to the lung base as seen in this patient. Additionally, tuberculomas do not contain fat density, as does the nodule in this patient.

【81】 Malignancy: A primary bronchogenic carcinoma or a single, isolated metastatic nodule would be differential considerations for the nodule seen on the CXR. However, metastases or primary bronchogenic carcinoma should not contain central fat density. Unless the patient has a history of a liposarcoma, the presence of internal fat density on CT excludes the diagnosis of malignancy.

【82】 Arteriovenous malformation: These are single in about two-thirds of cases, and may be included in the differential for a solitary pulmonary nodule. Feeding and draining vessels, which must be identified to make the diagnosis, may be difficult to visualize on plain radiographs. While this would be a possible diagnosis based on the radiograph, the absence of a feeding artery and draining vein on CT and the presence of central fat density exclude this as a possibility.

【83】DIAGNOSIS

【84】Hamartoma

【85】KEY FACTS

【86】Clinical

【87】 A hamartoma is a developmental malformation of disorganized tissues that normally constitute the organ in which the tumor occurs.

【88】 In the lung, these lesions are better regarded as benign neoplasms than as developmental malformations.

【89】 Peak incidence is in the sixth decade, and they are uncommon in patients <30 years of age.

【90】 Although they are uncommon pulmonary tumors, they are nevertheless the most common benign tumors of the lung.

【91】 They occur more commonly in males, with a male to female ratio between 2:1 and 3:1.

【92】 Pulmonary hamartomas are usually solitary, although multiple pulmonary hamartomas can occur rarely.

【93】 Multiple hamartoma syndrome (Cowden’s disease) is a rare autosomal dominant dermatosis, which is characterized by multiple mucocutaneous lesions and gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps; hamartomas of the lung occur only rarely in this disease.

【94】Radiologic

【95】 Hamartomas characteristically are well-defined solitary nodules that are usually <4 cm in diameter.

【96】 The majority are located peripherally (90%), although occasionally they may arise in the central bronchi.

【97】 Calcification is less commonly seen on radiographs than at pathology; the rate of calcification is variable in different series, from 5% to 50%. A popcorn pattern of calcification is considered diagnostic of hamartoma.

【98】 The presence of fat attenuation (with or without calcification) within the mass is best demonstrated on CT, and is also a diagnostic feature. Fat may be identified by CT density in the range of -40 to -120 HU.

【99】 Fat is not present in approximately one-third of hamartomas.

【100】 In patients with hamartomas without diagnostic imaging features, FDG-PET scan may be helpful. Ham-artomas generally do not demonstrate significant hypermetabolism, although mild FDG activity has been described. Occasionally, when there is mild FDG activity within the nodule, a percutaneous biopsy may need to be performed in order to obviate surgical biopsy.

【101】 In the small percentage of centrally occurring hamarto-mas, atelectasis and obstructive pneumonia may occur.

【113】 Arteriovenous malformation (AVM): The well-defined, lobulated contour, medial location, and identification of feeding and draining vessels are characteristic for this diagnosis.
